   127	/-! ## Reflections
   128	
   129	The *reflections* of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   130	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:228-250`, are the self-adjoint involutions attached to
   131	two-outcome projective measurements, which are exactly the binary observables
   132	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable` of
   133	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Defs.lean`.  The Magic Square rigidity
   134	argument therefore uses that predicate and its algebra directly:
   135	`IsBinaryObservable.one`, `IsBinaryObservable.mul`,
   136	`IsBinaryObservable.isometry`, `isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one` and
   137	`isBinaryObservable_one_heteroKron`. -/
   138	
   139	/-- Operators placed on the two tensor factors commute. -/
   140	theorem heteroKron_comm {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
   141	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] (X : Op ιA) (Y : Op ιB) :
   142	    heteroKron X (1 : Op ιB) * heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) Y =
   143	      heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) Y * heteroKron X (1 : Op ιB) := by
   144	  rw [heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one, one_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
   145	
   146	/-! ## Closeness in the state-dependent norm -/
   147	
   148	/-- Two operators are *close within `δ` on `ψ`* when the state-dependent norm of
   149	their difference is at most `δ`, that is, when the Euclidean distance between
   150	`M ψ` and `N ψ` is at most `δ`.
   151	
   152	This is **not** the relation `M ≈_δ N` of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   153	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:249`, paper
   154	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:644-646`: there the relation
   155	bounds the *squared* quantity `⟨ψ|(M - N)ᴴ (M - N)|ψ⟩` by `O(δ)`, and it is
   156	formalized in this development by `opDistSq` (`def:povm-distance`, blueprint
   157	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`).  The unsquared relation defined here is the one
   158	under which the triangle inequality is additive, which is what the
   159	solution-group computation of `Rigidity/Anticommutation.lean` iterates;
   160	`NormCloseOn.opDistSq_le` converts a bound at scale `δ` here into the bound `δ ^ 2`
   161	for `opDistSq`. -/
   162	def NormCloseOn {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   163	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) (M N : Op ι) : Prop :=
   164	  ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ≤ δ
   165	
   166	namespace NormCloseOn
   167	
   168	variable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   169	variable {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι} {δ η : ℝ} {M N P U : Op ι}
   170	
   171	/-- Equal operators are close at every nonnegative scale. -/
   172	theorem of_eq (h : M = N) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N := by
   173	  have hzero : applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ = 0 := by
   174	    rw [h, sub_self, applyOperatorToState_zero_op]
   175	  rw [NormCloseOn, hzero, norm_zero]
   176	  exact hδ
   177	
   178	/-- Closeness is symmetric. -/
   179	theorem symm (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) : NormCloseOn ψ δ N M := by
   180	  have happ : applyOperatorToState (N - M) ψ = -applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ := by
   181	    rw [show N - M = -(M - N) by abel]
   182	    unfold applyOperatorToState
   183	    simp only [map_neg, LinearMap.neg_apply]
   184	  rw [NormCloseOn, happ, norm_neg]
   185	  exact h
   186	
   187	/-- Enlarging the scale preserves closeness. -/
   188	theorem mono (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) (hδ : δ ≤ η) : NormCloseOn ψ η M N :=
   189	  le_trans h hδ
   190	
   191	/-- Closeness composes by the triangle inequality. -/
   192	theorem trans (h₁ : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) (h₂ : NormCloseOn ψ η N P) :
   193	    NormCloseOn ψ (δ + η) M P := by
   194	  have hsplit : M - P = (M - N) + (N - P) := by abel
   195	  calc ‖applyOperatorToState (M - P) ψ‖
   196	      = ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ + applyOperatorToState (N - P) ψ‖ := by
   197	        rw [hsplit, applyOperatorToState_add_op]
   198	    _ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ + ‖applyOperatorToState (N - P) ψ‖ :=
   199	        norm_add_le _ _
   200	    _ ≤ δ + η := add_le_add h₁ h₂
   201	
   202	/-- Multiplying on the left by an isometric operator preserves closeness. -/
   203	theorem isometry_mul (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) :
   204	    NormCloseOn ψ δ (U * M) (U * N) := by
   205	  have hsub : U * M - U * N = U * (M - N) := by noncomm_ring
   206	  rw [NormCloseOn, hsub, norm_applyOperatorToState_isometry_mul hU]
   207	  exact h
   208	
   209	/-- Negating both operators leaves the state-dependent norm of the difference
   210	unchanged. -/
   211	theorem neg (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) : NormCloseOn ψ δ (-M) (-N) := by
   212	  change ‖applyOperatorToState (-M - -N) ψ‖ ≤ δ
   213	  rw [show -M - -N = -(M - N) by abel]
   214	  have happ : applyOperatorToState (-(M - N)) ψ =
   215	      -applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ := by
   216	    unfold applyOperatorToState
   217	    simp only [map_neg, LinearMap.neg_apply]
   218	  rw [happ, norm_neg]
   219	  exact h
   220	
   221	/-- Multiplying both operators by a scalar of modulus one leaves the
   222	state-dependent norm of the difference unchanged. -/
   223	theorem smul {c : ℂ} (hc : ‖c‖ = 1) (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) :
   224	    NormCloseOn ψ δ (c • M) (c • N) := by
   225	  change ‖applyOperatorToState (c • M - c • N) ψ‖ ≤ δ
   226	  rw [← smul_sub, applyOperatorToState_smul, norm_smul, hc, one_mul]
   227	  exact h
   228	
   229	/-- Replacing the left factor of a product costs the distance between the two
   230	factors plus twice the cost of replacing the right factor by an operator
   231	commuting with both.  This is the mechanism by which a state-dependent relation
   232	is used in the middle of a word: the tail is first moved to the other player,
   233	where it commutes with everything acting on the first player. -/
   234	theorem mul_left_subst {X X' K K' : Op ι}
   235	    (hXX' : NormCloseOn ψ δ X X') (hKK' : NormCloseOn ψ η K K')
   236	    (hX : Xᴴ * X = 1) (hX' : X'ᴴ * X' = 1) (hK' : K'ᴴ * K' = 1)
   237	    (hcX : X * K' = K' * X) (hcX' : X' * K' = K' * X') :
   238	    NormCloseOn ψ (η + δ + η) (X * K) (X' * K) := by
   239	  have h1 : NormCloseOn ψ η (X * K) (X * K') := NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hX hKK'
   240	  have h2 : NormCloseOn ψ δ (X * K') (X' * K') := by
   241	    change ‖applyOperatorToState (X * K' - X' * K') ψ‖ ≤ δ
   242	    rw [show X * K' - X' * K' = K' * X - K' * X' by rw [hcX, hcX']]
   243	    exact NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hK' hXX'
   244	  have h3 : NormCloseOn ψ η (X' * K') (X' * K) := NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hX' hKK'.symm
   245	  exact (h1.trans h2).trans h3
   246	
   247	/-- Conversion to the state-dependent distance of the source: `M ≈_δ N` of
   248	`thm:ms-rigidity` (blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:249`, paper
   249	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:644-646`) bounds
   250	`⟨ψ|(M - N)ᴴ (M - N)|ψ⟩`, which is `opDistSq` on the one-point distribution
   251	(`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`).  A bound at
   252	scale `δ` for the unsquared relation is a bound at scale `δ ^ 2` for it. -/
   253	theorem opDistSq_le (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) :
   254	    opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => M) (fun _ => N) ψ ≤ δ ^ 2 := by
   255	  have hnorm : ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ≤ δ := h
   256	  have heq : opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => M) (fun _ => N) ψ =
   257	      ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   258	    rw [opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq, opFamilyDistSq_uniform_unit]
   259	    simp
   260	  rw [heq]
   261	  nlinarith [norm_nonneg (applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ)]
   262	
   263	end NormCloseOn
   264	
   265	/-! ## Sign observables of a projective measurement -/
   266	
   267	section SignObs
   268	
   269	variable {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   270	
   271	/-- The `±1`-valued observable attached to a measurement together with a binary
   272	relabelling of its answers: an answer labelled `0` carries the eigenvalue `1`
   273	and an answer labelled `1` carries the eigenvalue `-1`.  For the Magic Square
   274	these are the cell observables of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   275	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
   276	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
   277	noncomputable def signObs (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (f : α → ZMod 2) : Op d :=
   278	  ∑ a, (bitSign (f a) : ℂ) • M.effect a
   279	
   280	/-- The sign observable is the observable of the binary measurement obtained by

281	relabelling the answers. -/
   282	theorem signObs_eq_obsOf_postprocess (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   283	    (f : α → ZMod 2) : signObs M f = obsOf (M.postprocess f) := by
   284	  classical
   285	  have hcases : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x = 0 ∨ x = 1 := by decide
   286	  have key : ∀ a : α, (bitSign (f a) : ℂ) • M.effect a =
   287	      (if f a = 0 then M.effect a else 0) - (if f a = 1 then M.effect a else 0) := by
   288	    intro a
   289	    rcases hcases (f a) with h | h <;> rw [h] <;>
   290	      norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one, neg_one_smul]
   291	  rw [signObs, obsOf, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
   292	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter,
   293	    Finset.sum_filter, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   294	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => key a
   295	
   296	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   297	/-- Formalization-only: the effects of a projective measurement are mutually
   298	orthogonal, so two spectral combinations of them multiply coefficientwise. -/
   299	private theorem sum_smul_effect_mul (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   300	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (c e : α → ℂ) :
   301	    (∑ a, c a • M.effect a) * (∑ a, e a • M.effect a) =
   302	      ∑ a, (c a * e a) • M.effect a := by
   303	  classical
   304	  have horth : ∀ a b : α, a ≠ b → M.effect a * M.effect b = 0 := fun a b hab =>
   305	    mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family hM M.sum_le_one hab
   306	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   307	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   308	  have hidem : M.effect a * M.effect a = M.effect a := (hM a).isIdempotentElem
   309	  rw [Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_sum, Finset.smul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single a]
   310	  · rw [Matrix.mul_smul, smul_smul, hidem]
   311	  · intro b _ hba
   312	    rw [Matrix.mul_smul, horth a b (Ne.symm hba), smul_zero, smul_zero]
   313	  · intro ha
   314	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a) ha
   315	
   316	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   317	/-- Sign observables of one projective measurement multiply by adding their
   318	relabellings. -/
   319	theorem signObs_mul (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   320	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f g : α → ZMod 2) :
   321	    signObs M f * signObs M g = signObs M (fun a => f a + g a) := by
   322	  rw [signObs, signObs, sum_smul_effect_mul M hM, signObs]
   323	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   324	  rw [← Complex.ofReal_mul, ← bit_sign_add]
   325	
   326	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   327	/-- The sign observable of the zero relabelling is the identity. -/
   328	theorem signObs_const_zero (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
   329	    signObs M (fun _ => 0) = 1 := by
   330	  have hb : ((bitSign (0 : ZMod 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) = 1 := by norm_num [bitSign]
   331	  rw [signObs]
   332	  simp only [hb, one_smul]
   333	  exact M.sum_eq_one
   334	
   335	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   336	/-- A sign observable of a projective measurement is an involution. -/
   337	theorem signObs_mul_self (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   338	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
   339	    signObs M f * signObs M f = 1 := by
   340	  rw [signObs_mul M hM]
   341	  have hzero : (fun a => f a + f a) = fun _ : α => (0 : ZMod 2) := by
   342	    funext a
   343	    exact (by decide : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x + x = 0) (f a)
   344	  rw [hzero, signObs_const_zero]
   345	
   346	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   347	/-- A sign observable of a projective measurement is self-adjoint. -/
   348	theorem signObs_conjTranspose (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   349	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
   350	    (signObs M f)ᴴ = signObs M f := by
   351	  rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, signObs, star_sum]
   352	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   353	  rw [star_smul]
   354	  congr 1
   355	  · simp
   356	  · exact (hM a).isSelfAdjoint
   357	
   358	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   359	/-- A sign observable of a projective measurement is a binary observable, the
   360	reflection attached to the relabelling `f`. -/
   361	theorem isBinaryObservable_signObs (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   362	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
   363	    IsBinaryObservable (signObs M f) :=
   364	  ⟨signObs_conjTranspose M hM f, signObs_mul_self M hM f⟩
   365	
   366	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   367	/-- Sign observables of one projective measurement commute. -/
   368	theorem signObs_comm (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   369	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f g : α → ZMod 2) :
   370	    signObs M f * signObs M g = signObs M g * signObs M f := by
   371	  rw [signObs_mul M hM, signObs_mul M hM]
   372	  congr 1
   373	  funext a
   374	  exact add_comm _ _
   375	
   376	end SignObs

   378	/-! ## Deviation of joint spectral combinations on the strategy state -/
   379	
   380	section JointDefect
   381	
   382	/-- Formalization-only: scalars pass through the second tensor factor. -/
   383	theorem heteroKron_smul_right {ιA ιB : Type} (c : ℂ) (M : Op ιA) (N : Op ιB) :
   384	    heteroKron M (c • N) = c • heteroKron M N := by
   385	  unfold heteroKron
   386	  exact Matrix.kronecker_smul c M N
   387	
   388	/-- Formalization-only: a real spectral combination of the effects of a
   389	projective measurement is self-adjoint. -/
   390	private theorem sum_real_smul_effect_conjTranspose {α d : Type} [Fintype α]
   391	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   392	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (c : α → ℝ) :
   393	    (∑ a, ((c a : ℝ) : ℂ) • M.effect a)ᴴ = ∑ a, ((c a : ℝ) : ℂ) • M.effect a := by
   394	  rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, star_sum]
   395	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   396	  rw [star_smul]
   397	  congr 1
   398	  · simp
   399	  · exact (hM a).isSelfAdjoint
   400	
   401	/-- Formalization-only: the quadratic form of a real spectral combination on a
   402	state is the corresponding real combination of the individual quadratic
   403	forms. -/
   404	private theorem re_inner_apply_sum_real_smul {ι γ : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   405	    [Fintype γ] (r : γ → ℝ) (K : γ → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   406	    (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (∑ c, ((r c : ℝ) : ℂ) • K c) ψ)).re =
   407	      ∑ c, r c * (inner ℂ ψ (applyOperatorToState (K c) ψ)).re := by
   408	  rw [applyOperatorToState_sum, inner_sum, Complex.re_sum]
   409	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => ?_
   410	  rw [applyOperatorToState_smul, inner_smul_right]
   411	  simp
   412	
   413	variable {G : Game}
   414	
   415	/-- Formalization-only: the joint effects of the two players form a projective
   416	measurement on the composite space when both local measurements are
   417	projective. -/
   418	private noncomputable def jointMeasurement (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   419	    (y : G.QuestionB) :
   420	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB) (T.ιA × T.ιB) :=
   421	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   422	    (fun ab => heteroKron ((T.A x).effect ab.1) ((T.B y).effect ab.2))
   423	    (fun ab => kronecker_nonneg ((T.A x).pos ab.1) ((T.B y).pos ab.2))
   424	    (by
   425	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   426	      calc ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   427	            heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b)
   428	          = ∑ a : G.AnswerA, heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a)
   429	              (∑ b : G.AnswerB, (T.B y).effect b) := by
   430	            exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => (heteroKron_sum_right _ _).symm
   431	        _ = heteroKron (∑ a : G.AnswerA, (T.A x).effect a) (1 : Op T.ιB) := by
   432	            rw [(T.B y).sum_eq_one, heteroKron_sum_left]
   433	        _ = 1 := by rw [(T.A x).sum_eq_one, heteroKron_one_one])
   434	
   435	/-- Formalization-only: the effects of the joint measurement. -/
   436	private theorem jointMeasurement_effect (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   437	    (y : G.QuestionB) (ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB) :
   438	    (jointMeasurement T x y).effect ab =
   439	      heteroKron ((T.A x).effect ab.1) ((T.B y).effect ab.2) := rfl
   440	
   441	/-- Formalization-only: the quadratic form of a joint effect is the Born weight
   442	of the corresponding answer pair. -/
   443	private theorem re_inner_jointMeasurement_effect (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   444	    (y : G.QuestionB) (ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB) :
   445	    (inner ℂ T.ψ (applyOperatorToState ((jointMeasurement T x y).effect ab) T.ψ)).re =
   446	      outcomeWeight T x y ab.1 ab.2 := rfl
   447	
   448	/-- A real spectral combination of the joint effects deviates from zero, in the
   449	state-dependent norm, by at most the mass of the answer pairs carrying a nonzero
   450	coefficient, scaled by the squared coefficient bound.  This is the estimate that
   451	converts each Magic Square rejection mass into an operator bound;
   452	`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   453	theorem norm_apply_joint_defect_sq_le (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   454	    (y : G.QuestionB) (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.A x))
   455	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.B y))
   456	    (coef : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → ℝ) (E : G.AnswerA → G.AnswerB → Prop)
   457	    [DecidableRel E] (hbound : ∀ a b, coef a b ^ 2 ≤ 4)
   458	    (hsupp : ∀ a b, ¬ E a b → coef a b = 0) :
   459	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   460	        (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, ((coef a b : ℝ) : ℂ) •
   461	          heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b)) T.ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
   462	      4 * outcomeEventWeight T x y E := by
   463	  classical
   464	  set J := jointMeasurement T x y with hJ
   465	  have hJproj : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective J := fun ab =>
   466	    MakingMeasurementsProjective.isProj_kronecker (hA ab.1) (hB ab.2)
   467	  have hcollapse : (∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB, ((coef a b : ℝ) : ℂ) •
   468	      heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b)) =
   469	      ∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • J.effect ab := by
   470	    rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
   471	    rfl
   472	  have hsa : (∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • J.effect ab)ᴴ =
   473	      ∑ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB, ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • J.effect ab :=
   474	    sum_real_smul_effect_conjTranspose J hJproj (fun ab => coef ab.1 ab.2)
   475	  have hsq : ∀ ab : G.AnswerA × G.AnswerB,
   476	      ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * ((coef ab.1 ab.2 : ℝ) : ℂ) =
   477	        ((coef ab.1 ab.2 ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
   478	    intro ab
   479	    rw [← Complex.ofReal_mul, sq]
   480	  rw [hcollapse, norm_applyOperatorToState_sq, hsa,
   481	    sum_smul_effect_mul J hJproj]
   482	  simp only [hsq]
   483	  rw [re_inner_apply_sum_real_smul]

237 docs/PROOF_INTEGRITY.md
# Lean Proof Integrity Rules

This file is the **single source of truth** for proof integrity checks in this
repository. All CI workflows and review prompts should reference this file
rather than duplicating the rules inline.

> **Lean version**: 4.x (Lean 3 keywords like `constant` do not apply)

> **Companion document:** [`anti_patterns.md`](./anti_patterns.md) catalogues
> subtler proof-evasion patterns that pass every blocker check below yet still
> fail to prove the claimed mathematics (conclusion-shaped hypotheses,
> definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback branches, trivial default
> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).
> Consult it alongside this file during review.

> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a
> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`
> blocker below may be temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The
> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof
> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the
> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a
> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or
> conditional helper
> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.
> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge
> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.

---

## Blockers

These patterns **must** be resolved before merging.

### Direct proof holes

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `sorry` | Axiomatically closes any goal — the proof is incomplete |
| `admit` | Tactic alias for `sorry` |

### Kernel / type system bypasses

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `native_decide` | Relies on trusted native evaluation / compiler; banned in Mathlib for soundness and process reasons |
| `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce` | Type system bypass — can fabricate any proof term |
| `lcProof` | Low-level proof fabrication primitive — can prove `False` |
| `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat` | Kernel reduction primitives exploitable for unsound proofs |

### Axiom smuggling

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `axiom` declarations | Introduces unproven assumptions that could be inconsistent; must be explicitly justified |

When an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,
prefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`
declaration, and add a regression check (for example a
`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in
`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen
the axiomatic base.

This preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper
theorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a
caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a
proof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly
conditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement
faithful to the paper.

### Circular reasoning

Lean's kernel forbids literal declaration cycles, so focus on **mathematical
circularity**:

- Proofs that assume (or trivially reintroduce) the statement being proved as a
  local hypothesis, then immediately close the goal from that hypothesis
- Helper lemmas in the same file that essentially restate the main goal and are
  only used to prove that goal
- Local `have`/`let` bindings that are just the goal rephrased, used to solve
  the goal without any real argument
- Newly introduced `axiom` that makes a difficult statement trivially provable
  without connecting to existing Mathlib / core theorems
- Abuse of `unsafe` features to fabricate proofs instead of giving a genuine
  derivation
- `by exact h` where `h` came from an unjustified assumption identical to the
  goal

### Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)

Proofs that avoid grounding in Mathlib:

- Custom re-declarations of standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., re-proving
  `add_comm` instead of importing it)
- `axiom` or `sorry`-based helper lemmas for facts that already exist in
  Mathlib
- Chains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core
- `private` helper lemmas that duplicate Mathlib API (e.g., custom matrix
  transpose lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)
- Overly long proof chains replaceable by a single Mathlib lemma

When flagging, perform an actual lookup (grep, `#find?`, `exact?`,
`library_search`). If an equivalent exists, cite the Mathlib lemma and module
path. If not, state "no equivalent found" with search evidence.

### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization

This is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or
theorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,
making them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.

Signs to watch for:

- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,
  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's
  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)
- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types
  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions
- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical
  semantics (e.g., a "projective measurement" definition that does not enforce
  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)
- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be
  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything
- Definitions that "work" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to
  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,
  incompatible universes)

When reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of
this?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the
scaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks
progress rather than enabling it.

### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift

A theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker
if its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.
Changing a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is
strongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a
documented mathematical necessity.

The most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an
extra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional
theorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not
repair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named
`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,
generic `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those
assumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.

Conditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet
be closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a
named lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional
helper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named
obligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show
that it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or
`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled
blueprint theorem with `\leanok`.

Existing bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs
for reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a
strengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the
bridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is
to restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a
tracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.

Not every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed
to encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model
instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be
faithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These
conditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is
mathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate
step of the source proof.

For every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:

- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;
- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;
- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened
  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.

---

## Warnings

These should be flagged for review but may be acceptable with justification.

### Placeholder tactics

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`, `suggest` | Search tactics left as placeholders — replace with the concrete result |

### Safety / termination bypasses

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `unsafe def` | Bypasses Lean safety checks; should not appear in proof-relevant code |
| `partial def` | No termination proof required; unsound if used to build proof terms |
| `implemented_by` / `implementedBy` | Decouples runtime behavior from proven specification |

### Suspicious options

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `set_option maxHeartbeats 0` | Disables timeout — can hide non-terminating proofs |
| `set_option maxHeartbeats` with values >= 4,000,000 | 20x the default (200,000) — likely indicates an inefficient proof |
| `set_option maxRecDepth` with values >= 10,000 | May hide structural issues in proofs |

### Debug artifacts

| Pattern | Risk |
|---------|------|
| `dbg_trace` | Debug trace left in code |
| `stop` | Halts elaboration — development aid only |
| `#check`, `#eval`, `#print` in proof files | Debug commands that should be removed |

---

## How to use this file

**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read
[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a
proof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation
structure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why
conditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a
tracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.

**In CI review prompts**: Reference this file instead of inlining the rules:
```
Read `docs/PROOF_INTEGRITY.md` for the complete list of proof integrity
rules. Flag blockers as must-fix issues that should block merge.
Flag warnings as advisory — note them but acknowledge they may be
acceptable with justification.
```

**For manual review**: Use this as a checklist when reviewing Lean PRs.

**Updating rules**: Edit this file and all referencing workflows will
automatically pick up the changes.

Structures that satisfy none of the above are dead on arrival and must not
merge.

### Related issues

- [#1379] — live `*Statement` ledger (replaces closed [#449] / [#451])
- [#449] — historical paper-wide gap tracker (closed 2026-05-01)
- [#451] — historical bridge-hypothesis tracker (closed 2026-04-30)
- [#278] — the original "derive `PermInvState` internally" discussion

---

## Reviewer checklist

Use this alongside the blocker
list in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and the [`proof_frontier_review.md`](./proof_frontier_review.md)
checklist for structure fields. For any theorem or lemma that claims a paper
result, ask:

- [ ] **Hypothesis audit.** Does any hypothesis contain (up to `∃`/`∧`) the
      theorem's conclusion? If yes, that's A1 — reject or strengthen.
- [ ] **Definitional audit.** Is the proof `rfl` or a one-line `simp`? If
      yes, does the unfolded definition do the paper's math, or just match
      the shape of the conclusion? The latter is A2.
- [ ] **Domain audit.** Does the function have a fallback branch (`if
      eligible ... else default`)? If yes, does the theorem's signature
      require eligibility? If not, that's A3.
- [ ] **Witness audit.** Does the proof pick `x := default` for an
      existential named after a paper lemma? That's A4 unless the witness
      is genuinely unique-up-to-isomorphism.
- [ ] **Mathlib audit.** Is there a `private lemma` that duplicates a
      Mathlib fact? Run `exact?` / `apply?` / `#find` before accepting it
      (A5).
- [ ] **External-citation audit.** Does the proof consume a `*Statement` /
      `*Witness` / `*Package`? Is there a tracking issue that names its
      grounding plan (A6)?
- [ ] **Paper-faithfulness.** Does the Lean signature match the paper's
      statement, or does Lean sneak in extra hypotheses? Flag divergences
      as ⚠️S in [#1379].

A lemma that passes all of these is a proof. A lemma that fails one is
scaffolding, and should be labelled and tracked as such (don't tag with
`\leanok` until the gap is closed).

## CI prevention

Mechanical detection is possible for many of these patterns:

- **A1 (conclusion-shaped hypothesis).** Use
  `python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci` as the current
  report-only tripwire for the PR [#491] inline-existential mutation. It parses
  theorem/lemma headers and warns when an explicit existential hypothesis shares
  the conclusion's salient structure, while printing witness-adapter helpers
  separately. When [#438] lands (`\leanok` ↔ `sorryAx` drift), extend the same
  idea to all `\leanok`-tagged declarations: parse the hypothesis list; if any
  hypothesis's type (modulo `∃`/`∀`/`∧`) contains a prefix of the conclusion
  structure, warn.
- **A2 (definitional sleight).** Grep for `theorem <Name>.* := rfl` where
  `<Name>` has a blueprint `\lean{}` cross-reference. The only allowed cases
  are ones annotated with `@[paper_bookkeeping]` (proposed attribute) or in
  an allow-list.
- **A3 (zero-fallback).** Grep for identifier suffixes `fallback`, `or0`,
  `orDefault`, `placeholder`, `sentinel` in `Defs/*` files. Each should have
  a docstring citing the downstream eligibility precondition.
- **A4 (default witnesses).** Grep `:= default`, `refine ⟨default`, `exact
  ⟨default`, `Classical.arbitrary` inside proof bodies (not typeclass
  definitions). Cross-reference to [#1379]'s witness ledger.
- **A5 (Mathlib bypass).** No reliable CI check, but `audits/` reports
  catch it during per-chapter audits.
- **A6 (external smuggles).** Every new `structure *Statement` without a
  producing theorem should be required to carry a `/-- Grounded by: #NNN
  -/` docstring, enforced by a lint rule over `blueprint/`.

The scripts in `scripts/` (notably `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py` and
`scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py`) are the natural home for extensions that
add these checks.

  [`project_conventions.md`](./project_conventions.md).

     6	Every question of the projectively dilated Magic Square strategy carries a

   295	/-- The sum of the three answer bits reported for a constraint question, with
   296	malformed answers contributing zero. -/
   297	def constraintBitSum (a : MsAnswer) : ZMod 2 :=
   298	  constraintBitOrZero 0 a + constraintBitOrZero 1 a + constraintBitOrZero 2 a
   299	
   300	/-- An answer whose three reported bits do not sum to the prescribed parity is a
   301	parity failure in the sense of the value-to-parity layer. -/
   302	theorem constraintParityFailure_of_bitSum_ne (i : Fin 6) (a : MsAnswer)
   303	    (h : constraintBitSum a ≠ msParity i) : ConstraintParityFailure i a := by
   304	  cases a with
   305	  | bit γ => exact wrong_constraint_answer_implies_parity_failure i (MsAnswer.bit γ) rfl
   306	  | triple β =>
   307	      intro hprod
   308	      apply h
   309	      have hsum : bitSign (∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = bitSign (msParity i) := by
   310	        rw [bit_sign_sum_fin_three]
   311	        exact hprod
   312	      have hbit := bit_sign_injective hsum
   313	      rw [Fin.sum_univ_three] at hbit
   314	      exact hbit
   315	
   316	/-- The product of Alice's three cell reflections of a constraint question is
   317	the reflection attached to the sum of the three reported bits. -/
   318	theorem msCellObsA_prod (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) :
   319	    msCellObsA S i 0 * msCellObsA S i 1 * msCellObsA S i 2 =
   320	      heteroKron (signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i))
   321	        constraintBitSum) 1 := by
   322	  rw [msCellObsA, msCellObsA, msCellObsA, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
   323	    signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A S _),
   324	    signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A S _), mul_one, one_mul]
   325	  rfl

   328	reflection attached to the sum of the three reported bits. -/
   329	theorem msCellObsB_prod (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) :
   330	    msCellObsB S i 0 * msCellObsB S i 1 * msCellObsB S i 2 =
   331	      heteroKron 1 (signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).B (MsType.constraint i))
   332	        constraintBitSum) := by
   333	  rw [msCellObsB, msCellObsB, msCellObsB, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
   334	    signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_B S _),
   335	    signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_B S _), mul_one, one_mul]
   336	  rfl

   338	/-- Formalization-only: nonnegativity of Alice's marginal event mass. -/
   339	private theorem alice_event_weight_nonneg (T : Strategy msGame) (x : MsType)
   340	    (E : MsAnswer → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : 0 ≤ aliceEventWeight T x E := by
   341	  rw [← outcome_event_weight_left_eq T x x E]
   342	  exact outcome_event_weight_nonneg T x x _
   343	
   344	/-- Formalization-only: nonnegativity of Bob's marginal event mass. -/
   345	private theorem bob_event_weight_nonneg (T : Strategy msGame) (y : MsType)
   346	    (E : MsAnswer → Prop) [DecidablePred E] : 0 ≤ bobEventWeight T y E := by
   347	  rw [← outcome_event_weight_right_eq T y y E]
   348	  exact outcome_event_weight_nonneg T y y _

   350	/-- Each of the six row and column relations holds for Alice's cell reflections

351	on the dilated state, with the sign prescribed by the corresponding linear
   352	equation and with error `12 * sqrt ε`.  This is the first operator consequence
   353	of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   354	theorem msCellObsA_prod_close (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
   355	    (i : Fin 6) :
   356	    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε)
   357	      (msCellObsA S i 0 * msCellObsA S i 1 * msCellObsA S i 2)
   358	      (((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • 1) := by
   359	  classical
   360	  have hsq := norm_alice_signObs_sub_const_sq_le (msDilatedStrategy S)
   361	    (MsType.constraint i) (MsType.constraint i)
   362	    (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A S _) (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_B S _)
   363	    constraintBitSum (msParity i)
   364	  rw [← msCellObsA_prod] at hsq
   365	  refine normCloseOn_of_sq_le hsq (alice_event_weight_nonneg _ _ _) ?_
   366	  calc aliceEventWeight (msDilatedStrategy S) (MsType.constraint i)
   367	        (fun a => constraintBitSum a ≠ msParity i)
   368	      ≤ aliceEventWeight (msDilatedStrategy S) (MsType.constraint i)
   369	          (ConstraintParityFailure i) :=
   370	        alice_event_weight_mono _ _ _ _ fun a ha =>
   371	          constraintParityFailure_of_bitSum_ne i a ha
   372	    _ = aliceParityFailureMass S i := ms_dilated_strategy_alice_parity_failure_mass S i
   373	    _ ≤ 36 * ε := alice_parity_failure_mass_le S ε hwin i
   374	
   375	/-- Each of the six row and column relations holds for Bob's cell reflections on
   376	the dilated state, with the sign prescribed by the corresponding linear equation
   377	and with error `12 * sqrt ε`. -/
   378	theorem msCellObsB_prod_close (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
   379	    (i : Fin 6) :
   380	    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε)
   381	      (((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • 1)
   382	      (msCellObsB S i 0 * msCellObsB S i 1 * msCellObsB S i 2) := by
   383	  classical
   384	  have hsq := norm_bob_signObs_sub_const_sq_le (msDilatedStrategy S)
   385	    (MsType.constraint i) (MsType.constraint i)
   386	    (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A S _) (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_B S _)
   387	    constraintBitSum (msParity i)
   388	  rw [← msCellObsB_prod] at hsq
   389	  refine normCloseOn_of_sq_le hsq (bob_event_weight_nonneg _ _ _) ?_

   391	        (fun b => msParity i ≠ constraintBitSum b)
   392	      ≤ bobEventWeight (msDilatedStrategy S) (MsType.constraint i)
   393	          (ConstraintParityFailure i) :=
   394	        bob_event_weight_mono _ _ _ _ fun b hb =>
   395	          constraintParityFailure_of_bitSum_ne i b (Ne.symm hb)
   396	    _ = bobParityFailureMass S i := ms_dilated_strategy_bob_parity_failure_mass S i
   397	    _ ≤ 36 * ε := bob_parity_failure_mass_le S ε hwin i

   446	      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a) :

   448	      heteroKron (signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i))

   573	theorem msLogicalZA_comm_msLogicalZB (S : Strategy msGame) :
   574	    msLogicalZA S * msLogicalZB S = msLogicalZB S * msLogicalZA S :=
   575	  msVarObsA_comm_msVarObsB S 4 4

   577	/-! ## Unit scalars -/
   578	
   579	/-- The sign of a binary value has modulus one as a complex number. -/
   580	theorem norm_bitSign_ofReal (c : ZMod 2) : ‖((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ = 1 := by
   581	  rw [Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs]
   582	  rcases bit_sign_eq_one_or_neg_one c with h | h <;> rw [h] <;> norm_num
   583	
   584	/-- The square of the sign of a binary value is one. -/
   585	theorem bitSign_ofReal_mul_self (c : ZMod 2) :
   586	    ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) * ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) = 1 := by
   587	  rw [← Complex.ofReal_mul]
   588	  rcases bit_sign_eq_one_or_neg_one c with h | h <;> rw [h] <;> norm_num
   589	
   590	/-- Formalization-only: a sign multiple of an isometric operator is
   591	isometric. -/
   592	private theorem isometry_bitSign_smul {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   593	    {c : ZMod 2} {U : Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) :
   594	    (((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • U)ᴴ * (((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • U) = 1 := by
   595	  have hstar : (((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • U)ᴴ = ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • Uᴴ := by
   596	    rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, star_smul, Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose]
   597	    congr 1
   598	    simp
   599	  rw [hstar, Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_smul, smul_smul, hU,
   600	    bitSign_ofReal_mul_self, one_smul]

   602	/-! ## Building blocks of the solution-group computation -/
   603	
   604	/-- One of Bob's three cell reflections of a constraint question is close, on
   605	the dilated state, to the signed product of the other two. -/
   606	theorem msCellObsB_single_close (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
   607	    (i : Fin 6) (k₀ k₁ k₂ : Fin 3)
   608	    (hsum : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero k₀ a + constraintBitOrZero k₁ a +
   609	      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a) :
   610	    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) (msCellObsB S i k₁)
   611	      (((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) •
   612	        (msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₂)) := by
   613	  have hprod := msCellObsB_prod_close_of S ε hwin i k₀ k₁ k₂ hsum
   614	  have hX2 : msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₀ = 1 :=
   615	    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S i k₀).mul_self_eq_one
   616	  have hZ2 : msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₂ = 1 :=
   617	    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S i k₂).mul_self_eq_one
   618	  have hZY : msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₁ =
   619	      msCellObsB S i k₁ * msCellObsB S i k₂ := msCellObsB_comm S i k₂ k₁
   620	  have hZX : msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀ =
   621	      msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₂ := msCellObsB_comm S i k₂ k₀
   622	  have hU : (msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀)ᴴ *
   623	      (msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀) = 1 :=
   624	    ((isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S i k₂).mul
   625	      (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S i k₀) hZX).isometry
   626	  have e1 : (msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀) *
   627	      (msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₁ * msCellObsB S i k₂) = msCellObsB S i k₁ := by
   628	    calc (msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀) *
   629	          (msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₁ * msCellObsB S i k₂)
   630	        = msCellObsB S i k₂ *
   631	            ((msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₀) * msCellObsB S i k₁) *
   632	            msCellObsB S i k₂ := by noncomm_ring
   633	      _ = msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₁ * msCellObsB S i k₂ := by
   634	          rw [hX2, one_mul]
   635	      _ = msCellObsB S i k₁ * msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₂ := by rw [hZY]
   636	      _ = msCellObsB S i k₁ := by rw [mul_assoc, hZ2, mul_one]
   637	  have e2 : (msCellObsB S i k₂ * msCellObsB S i k₀) *
   638	      (((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op _)) =
   639	      ((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • (msCellObsB S i k₀ * msCellObsB S i k₂) := by
   640	    rw [Matrix.mul_smul, mul_one, hZX]
   641	  have h := NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hU hprod
   642	  rw [e1, e2] at h
   643	  exact h.symm
   644	
   645	/-- A product of two of Bob's cell reflections is close, on the dilated state,
   646	to the product of Alice's variable reflections at the same two cells, taken in
   647	the reverse order. -/
   648	theorem msCellObsB_mul_close (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
   649	    (I J : Fin 6) (k l : Fin 3) :
   650	    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε + 12 * Real.sqrt ε)
   651	      (msCellObsB S I k * msCellObsB S J l)
   652	      (msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l) * msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars I k)) := by
   653	  have p1 : NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) (msCellObsB S J l)
   654	      (msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l)) :=
   655	    (msVarObsA_close_msCellObsB S ε hwin J l).symm
   656	  have p2 : NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) (msCellObsB S I k)
   657	      (msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars I k)) :=
   658	    (msVarObsA_close_msCellObsB S ε hwin I k).symm
   659	  have h1 : NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε)
   660	      (msCellObsB S I k * msCellObsB S J l)
   661	      (msCellObsB S I k * msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l)) :=
   662	    NormCloseOn.isometry_mul (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S I k).isometry p1
   663	  have hswap : msCellObsB S I k * msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l) =
   664	      msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l) * msCellObsB S I k :=
   665	    (msVarObsA_comm_msCellObsB S (msConstraintVars J l) I k).symm
   666	  rw [hswap] at h1
   667	  exact h1.trans (NormCloseOn.isometry_mul (isBinaryObservable_msVarObsA S _).isometry p2)
   668	
   669	/-- Two of Bob's cell reflections attached to a common cell by two different
   670	constraint questions are close on the dilated state. -/
   671	theorem msCellObsB_close_of_same_cell (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
   672	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) (I J : Fin 6) (k l : Fin 3)
   673	    (hcell : msConstraintVars I k = msConstraintVars J l) :
   674	    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε + 12 * Real.sqrt ε)
   675	      (msCellObsB S I k) (msCellObsB S J l) := by
   676	  have p1 : NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) (msCellObsB S I k)
   677	      (msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars I k)) :=
   678	    (msVarObsA_close_msCellObsB S ε hwin I k).symm
   679	  have p2 : NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε)
   680	      (msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l)) (msCellObsB S J l) :=
   681	    msVarObsA_close_msCellObsB S ε hwin J l
   682	  rw [hcell] at p1
   683	  exact p1.trans p2
   684	
   685	end

     3	/-!
     4	# Approximate anticommutation in the Magic Square game
     5	
     6	The Magic Square is the smallest linear constraint system whose solution group
     7	forces two of its generators to anticommute.  This file carries out that
     8	computation on the projective dilation of an arbitrary strategy, in the
     9	state-dependent norm and with explicit constants.
    10	
    11	The computation proceeds in three identical steps.  Each step takes two
    12	constraints sharing exactly one cell and rewrites a product of two cell
    13	reflections, one from each constraint, as the signed product of the two
    14	reflections at the remaining cells.  Iterating the step around the grid returns
    15	to the pair one started from, in the opposite order and with the sign reversed
    16	by the exceptional parity of the third column; this yields the approximate
    17	anticommutation of the two reflections at the cells labelled by the paper's
    18	first and fifth variables.
    19	
    20	## References
    21	
    22	The statement supported here is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
    23	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
    24	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
    25	proved in Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9; the argument
    26	below is the Magic Square instance of the solution-group computation used there
    27	(their Figure describing the generators of the solution group).  The variable
    28	and constraint indices are zero-based, so the paper's first and fifth variables
    29	are the cells `0` and `4`.
    30	-/
    31	
    32	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    33	
    34	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity
    35	
    36	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-! ## Placement of an operator on one player's tensor factor -/
    41	
    42	/-- Formalization-only: an operator acting on Alice's tensor factor alone. -/
    43	private def AlicePlaced {ιA ιB : Type} [DecidableEq ιB] (Z : Op (ιA × ιB)) : Prop :=
    44	  ∃ M : Op ιA, Z = heteroKron M 1
    45	
    46	/-- Formalization-only: an operator acting on Bob's tensor factor alone. -/
    47	private def BobPlaced {ιA ιB : Type} [DecidableEq ιA] (Z : Op (ιA × ιB)) : Prop :=
    48	  ∃ N : Op ιB, Z = heteroKron 1 N
    49	
    50	/-- Formalization-only: operators of the two players commute. -/
    51	private theorem AlicePlaced.comm {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    52	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] {Z W : Op (ιA × ιB)} (hZ : AlicePlaced Z)
    53	    (hW : BobPlaced W) : Z * W = W * Z := by
    54	  obtain ⟨M, rfl⟩ := hZ
    55	  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := hW
    56	  exact heteroKron_comm M N
    57	
    58	/-- Formalization-only: products stay on Alice's tensor factor. -/
    59	private theorem AlicePlaced.mul {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA]
    60	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] {Z W : Op (ιA × ιB)} (hZ : AlicePlaced Z)
    61	    (hW : AlicePlaced W) : AlicePlaced (Z * W) := by
    62	  obtain ⟨M, rfl⟩ := hZ
    63	  obtain ⟨M', rfl⟩ := hW
    64	  exact ⟨M * M', by rw [heteroKron_mul, mul_one]⟩
    65	
    66	/-- Formalization-only: products stay on Bob's tensor factor. -/
    67	private theorem BobPlaced.mul {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    68	    [Fintype ιB] {Z W : Op (ιA × ιB)} (hZ : BobPlaced Z)
    69	    (hW : BobPlaced W) : BobPlaced (Z * W) := by
    70	  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := hZ
    71	  obtain ⟨N', rfl⟩ := hW
    72	  exact ⟨N * N', by rw [heteroKron_mul, mul_one]⟩
    73	
    74	/-- Formalization-only: scalar multiples stay on Bob's tensor factor. -/
    75	private theorem BobPlaced.smul {ιA ιB : Type} [DecidableEq ιA] {c : ℂ} {Z : Op (ιA × ιB)}
    76	    (hZ : BobPlaced Z) : BobPlaced (c • Z) := by
    77	  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := hZ
    78	  exact ⟨c • N, (heteroKron_smul_right c 1 N).symm⟩
    79	
    80	/-- Formalization-only: operators of the two players commute. -/
    81	private theorem BobPlaced.comm {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    82	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] {Z W : Op (ιA × ιB)} (hZ : BobPlaced Z)
    83	    (hW : AlicePlaced W) : Z * W = W * Z := (hW.comm hZ).symm
    84	
    85	/-- Formalization-only: scalar multiples stay on Alice's tensor factor. -/
    86	private theorem AlicePlaced.smul {ιA ιB : Type} [DecidableEq ιB] {c : ℂ}
    87	    {Z : Op (ιA × ιB)} (hZ : AlicePlaced Z) : AlicePlaced (c • Z) := by
    88	  obtain ⟨M, rfl⟩ := hZ
    89	  exact ⟨c • M, (heteroKron_smul_left c M 1).symm⟩
    90	
    91	/-- Alice's cell reflection acts on her tensor factor alone. -/
    92	private theorem alicePlaced_msCellObsA (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    93	    AlicePlaced (msCellObsA S i k) := ⟨_, rfl⟩

    99	/-- Alice's variable reflection acts on her tensor factor alone. -/
   100	private theorem alicePlaced_msVarObsA (S : Strategy msGame) (j : Fin 9) :
   101	    AlicePlaced (msVarObsA S j) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
   102	
   103	/-- Bob's cell reflection acts on his tensor factor alone. -/
   104	private theorem bobPlaced_msCellObsB (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
   105	    BobPlaced (msCellObsB S i k) := ⟨_, rfl⟩

   107	/-! ## Isometry bookkeeping -/
   108	
   109	/-- Formalization-only: a product of isometric operators is isometric. -/
   110	private theorem isometry_mul_isometry {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   111	    {U V : Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) (hV : Vᴴ * V = 1) : (U * V)ᴴ * (U * V) = 1 := by
   112	  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul]
   113	  calc Vᴴ * Uᴴ * (U * V) = Vᴴ * (Uᴴ * U) * V := by noncomm_ring
   114	    _ = 1 := by rw [hU, mul_one, hV]
   115	
   116	/-- Formalization-only: a unit scalar multiple of an isometric operator is
   117	isometric. -/
   118	private theorem isometry_smul {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {c : ℂ}
   119	    (hstar : star c = c) (hsq : c * c = 1) {U : Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) :
   120	    (c • U)ᴴ * (c • U) = 1 := by
   121	  have hstarT : (c • U)ᴴ = c • Uᴴ := by
   122	    rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, star_smul, Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, hstar]
   123	  rw [hstarT, Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_smul, smul_smul, hU, hsq, one_smul]
   124	
   125	/-- The complex sign of a binary value is fixed by conjugation. -/
   126	theorem star_bitSign_ofReal (c : ZMod 2) :
   127	    star ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) = ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
   128	  simp
   129	
   130	/-! ## One step of the solution-group computation -/
   131	
   132	/-- One step of the Magic Square solution-group computation.  Here `X`, `Y`, `W`
   133	are three reflections of one player attached to a single constraint, with `X`
   134	and `W` commuting and `Y` close to the signed product `sI • (X * W)` prescribed
   135	by that constraint; the reflections `P`, `Q`, `R` play the same role for a
   136	second constraint with sign `sJ`.  The reflections `Pa` and `Ra` are the
   137	counterparts of `P` and `R` on the other player, and `P` is close to `X` because
   138	the two constraints share the cell that `X` and `P` are attached to.  The
   139	conclusion rewrites the product `Y * Q` as the signed product of the two
   140	remaining reflections.  Formalization-only support for `thm:ms-rigidity`,
   141	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   142	private theorem normCloseOn_step {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
   143	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)} {δ : ℝ}
   144	    {X Y W P Q R Pa Ra : Op (ιA × ιB)} {sI sJ : ℂ}
   145	    (hXr : IsBinaryObservable X) (hYr : IsBinaryObservable Y) (hWr : IsBinaryObservable W)
   146	    (hPr : IsBinaryObservable P)
   147	    (hPar : IsBinaryObservable Pa) (hRar : IsBinaryObservable Ra)
   148	    (hcY : Y * (Ra * Pa) = (Ra * Pa) * Y)
   149	    (hcXW : (X * W) * (Ra * Pa) = (Ra * Pa) * (X * W))
   150	    (hcP : P * Ra = Ra * P) (hcX : X * Ra = Ra * X)
   151	    (hXW : X * W = W * X)
   152	    (hsJnorm : ‖sJ‖ = 1) (hsIstar : star sI = sI) (hsIsq : sI * sI = 1)
   153	    (hQ : NormCloseOn ψ δ Q (sJ • (P * R)))
   154	    (hY : NormCloseOn ψ δ Y (sI • (X * W)))
   155	    (hPPa : NormCloseOn ψ δ P Pa) (hRRa : NormCloseOn ψ δ R Ra)
   156	    (hPX : NormCloseOn ψ (δ + δ) P X) :
   157	    NormCloseOn ψ (10 * δ) (Y * Q) ((sI * sJ) • (W * R)) := by
   158	  have hPRa : NormCloseOn ψ (δ + δ) (P * R) (Ra * Pa) := by
   159	    have s1 : NormCloseOn ψ δ (P * R) (P * Ra) := NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hPr.isometry hRRa
   160	    rw [show P * Ra = Ra * P from hcP] at s1
   161	    exact s1.trans (NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hRar.isometry hPPa)
   162	  have hRaPa : (Ra * Pa)ᴴ * (Ra * Pa) = 1 :=
   163	    isometry_mul_isometry hRar.isometry hPar.isometry
   164	  have hXWiso : (X * W)ᴴ * (X * W) = 1 := isometry_mul_isometry hXr.isometry hWr.isometry
   165	  have hsXWiso : (sI • (X * W))ᴴ * (sI • (X * W)) = 1 :=
   166	    isometry_smul hsIstar hsIsq hXWiso
   167	  have hcsXW : (sI • (X * W)) * (Ra * Pa) = (Ra * Pa) * (sI • (X * W)) := by
   168	    rw [Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_smul, hcXW]
   169	  have h2 : NormCloseOn ψ (δ + δ + δ + (δ + δ)) (Y * (P * R)) ((sI • (X * W)) * (P * R)) :=
   170	    NormCloseOn.mul_left_subst hY hPRa hYr.isometry hsXWiso hRaPa hcY hcsXW
   171	  have hPRXR : NormCloseOn ψ (δ + (δ + δ) + δ) (P * R) (X * R) :=
   172	    NormCloseOn.mul_left_subst hPX hRRa hPr.isometry hXr.isometry hRar.isometry hcP hcX
   173	  have h3 : NormCloseOn ψ (δ + (δ + δ) + δ)
   174	      ((sI • (X * W)) * (P * R)) ((sI • (X * W)) * (X * R)) :=
   175	    NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hsXWiso hPRXR
   176	  have e2 : (sI • (X * W)) * (X * R) = sI • (W * R) := by
   177	    rw [Matrix.smul_mul]
   178	    congr 1
   179	    calc (X * W) * (X * R) = X * (W * X) * R := by noncomm_ring
   180	      _ = X * (X * W) * R := by rw [hXW]
   181	      _ = (X * X) * (W * R) := by noncomm_ring
   182	      _ = W * R := by rw [hXr.mul_self_eq_one, one_mul]
   183	  have hA : NormCloseOn ψ δ (Y * Q) (sJ • (Y * (P * R))) := by
   184	    have h1 : NormCloseOn ψ δ (Y * Q) (Y * (sJ • (P * R))) :=
   185	      NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hYr.isometry hQ
   186	    rwa [Matrix.mul_smul] at h1
   187	  have hB := NormCloseOn.smul hsJnorm h2
   188	  have hC := NormCloseOn.smul hsJnorm h3
   189	  have e3 : sJ • ((sI • (X * W)) * (X * R)) = (sI * sJ) • (W * R) := by
   190	    rw [e2, smul_smul, mul_comm]
   191	  have hfinal := (hA.trans hB).trans hC
   192	  rw [e3] at hfinal
   193	  exact hfinal.mono (by linarith)
   194	
   195	/-! ## Negation and the sign of a constraint -/
   196	
   197	/-- Formalization-only: closeness to a negative is symmetric in the two
   198	operators. -/
   199	private theorem normCloseOn_neg_swap {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   200	    {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι} {δ : ℝ} {M N : Op ι} (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M (-N)) :
   201	    NormCloseOn ψ δ N (-M) := by
   202	  change ‖applyOperatorToState (N - -M) ψ‖ ≤ δ
   203	  rw [show N - -M = M - -N by abel]
   204	  exact h
   205	
   206	/-! ## The Magic Square instance of one step -/
   207	
   208	/-- One step of the solution-group computation for Bob's cell reflections: for
   209	two constraints sharing the cell at positions `k₀` and `l₀`, the product of the
   210	reflections at the positions `k₁` and `l₁` is close to the signed product of the
   211	reflections at the two remaining positions. -/
   212	theorem msCellObsB_step (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
   213	    (I J : Fin 6) (k₀ k₁ k₂ l₀ l₁ l₂ : Fin 3)
   214	    (hI : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero k₀ a + constraintBitOrZero k₁ a +
   215	      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a)
   216	    (hJ : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero l₀ a + constraintBitOrZero l₁ a +

     4	/-!
     5	# Magic Square value-to-parity relations
     6	
     7	This file extracts the elementary probability relations used at the start of
     8	the Magic Square rigidity argument.  A strategy of value at least `1 - ε` has
     9	total rejection mass at most `ε`.  Since the question distribution is
    10	supported on at most 36 directed incidences, the rejection mass at each
    11	incidence is at most `36 * ε`.  This controls malformed answers, consistency
    12	of the two reported bits at every cell, and the parity product on each of the
    13	six row or column constraints.
    14	
    15	The arguments apply to arbitrary finite POVMs.  In particular, malformed
    16	answers remain in the event masses when `msBitOrZero` and
    17	`constraintBitOrZero` turn the common answer alphabet into binary outcomes.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	The Magic Square game is defined in
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`
    23	and `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:201-222`.  These relations are the
    24	probabilistic input to the rigidity result cited at paper lines 612-652 from
    25	Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    29	
    30	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity
    31	
    32	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    33	
    34	noncomputable section
    35	
    36	/-! ## The directed incidence distribution -/
    37	
    38	/-- The 36 possible directed constraint-variable incidences. -/
    39	def directedIncidence : ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool) → MsType × MsType
    40	  | ((i, k), false) => (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k))
    41	  | ((i, k), true) => (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i)
    42	
    43	/-- Every question pair in the Magic Square distribution is a directed incidence. -/
    44	theorem ms_support_subset_directed_incidences :
    45	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support ⊆
    46	      (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image directedIncidence := by
    47	  intro xy hxy
    48	  have hedge : Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges :=
    49	    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hxy).2
    50	  rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hedge with ⟨ik, _hik, heq⟩
    51	  have heq' :
    52	      ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) = xy ∨
    53	        ((.constraint ik.1, .var (msConstraintVars ik.1 ik.2)) : MsType × MsType) =
    54	          xy.swap :=
    55	    (Sym2.mk_eq_mk_iff (α := MsType)).mp heq
    56	  rcases heq' with heq' | heq'
    57	  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, false), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    58	    simpa [directedIncidence] using heq'
    59	  · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(ik, true), Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    60	    simpa [directedIncidence] using congrArg Prod.swap heq'
    61	
    62	/-- The Magic Square question distribution has at most 36 support points. -/
    63	theorem ms_support_card_le :
    64	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤ 36 := by
    65	  calc
    66	    (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card ≤
    67	        ((Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).image
    68	          directedIncidence).card :=
    69	      Finset.card_le_card ms_support_subset_directed_incidences
    70	    _ ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset ((Fin 6 × Fin 3) × Bool)).card :=
    71	      Finset.card_image_le
    72	    _ = 36 := by norm_num
    73	
    74	/-- A constraint-to-variable incidence belongs to the question support. -/
    75	theorem ms_forward_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    76	    (.constraint i, .var (msConstraintVars i k)) ∈
    77	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
    78	  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    79	  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    80	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    81	
    82	/-- A variable-to-constraint incidence belongs to the question support. -/
    83	theorem ms_reverse_incidence_mem_support (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
    84	    (.var (msConstraintVars i k), .constraint i) ∈
    85	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support := by
    86	  apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    87	  refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ?_⟩
    88	  rw [Sym2.eq_swap]
    89	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i, k), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    90	
    91	/-- Every supported question pair has probability at least `1 / 36`. -/
    92	theorem ms_question_weight_ge {xy : MsType × MsType}
    93	    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :
    94	    (1 : ℝ) / 36 ≤ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy := by
    95	  have hmemFilter :
    96	      xy ∈ ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
    97	        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges) := hxy
    98	  rw [show (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy =
    99	      1 / ((graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support.card : ℝ) by
   100	    change (Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   101	        ((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
   102	          Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges)).weight xy =
   103	      1 / (((Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter fun ab =>
   104	        Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ msEdges).card : ℝ)
   105	    rw [Distribution.uniformOnFinset_weight, if_pos hmemFilter]]
   106	  apply one_div_le_one_div_of_le
   107	  · exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨xy, hxy⟩
   108	  · exact_mod_cast ms_support_card_le

   110	/-! ## Rejection mass from the game value -/
   111	
   112	/-- The rejection mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
   113	noncomputable def rejectionMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) : ℝ :=
   114	  outcomeEventWeight S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = false
   115	
   116	/-- The acceptance mass conditioned on a question pair. -/
   117	noncomputable def acceptanceMass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) : ℝ :=
   118	  outcomeEventWeight S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = true
   119	
   120	/-- The rejection mass averaged over the Magic Square question distribution. -/
   121	noncomputable def totalRejectionMass (S : Strategy msGame) : ℝ :=
   122	  avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) fun xy =>
   123	    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2
   124	
   125	/-- Acceptance and rejection partition the conditioned answer mass. -/
   126	theorem acceptance_mass_add_rejection_mass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) :
   127	    acceptanceMass S x y + rejectionMass S x y = 1 := by
   128	  rw [← show (∑ a : MsAnswer, ∑ b : MsAnswer, outcomeWeight S x y a b) = 1 by
   129	    exact outcomeWeight_sum_eq_one S x y]
   130	  unfold acceptanceMass rejectionMass outcomeEventWeight
   131	  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   132	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   133	  intro a _
   134	  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   135	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   136	  intro b _
   137	  cases h : msWinPredicate x y a b <;> simp [h]
   138	
   139	/-- The strategy value is the average conditioned acceptance mass. -/
   140	theorem strategy_value_eq_acceptance_mass (S : Strategy msGame) :
   141	    S.value = avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) fun xy =>
   142	      acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2 := by
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	/-- Total rejection mass is exactly one minus the strategy value. -/
   146	theorem total_rejection_mass_eq_one_sub_value (S : Strategy msGame) :
   147	    totalRejectionMass S = 1 - S.value := by
   148	  rw [show S.value = avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   149	      acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) by rfl]
   150	  unfold totalRejectionMass
   151	  calc
   152	    avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   153	        rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2) =
   154	        avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   155	          1 - acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) := by
   156	      apply avgOver_congr
   157	      intro xy
   158	      linarith [show acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2 + rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 = 1 by
   159	        exact acceptance_mass_add_rejection_mass S xy.1 xy.2]
   160	    _ = avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun _ => 1) -
   161	        avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   162	          acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) := avgOver_sub _ _ _
   163	    _ = 1 - avgOver (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty) (fun xy =>
   164	        acceptanceMass S xy.1 xy.2) := by
   165	      rw [avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (by
   166	        unfold graphDistribution
   167	        apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   168	        refine ⟨(.constraint 0, .var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
   169	        simp [msEdges])]
   170	
   171	/-- Total rejection mass is nonnegative. -/
   172	theorem total_rejection_mass_nonneg (S : Strategy msGame) :
   173	    0 ≤ totalRejectionMass S := by
   174	  unfold totalRejectionMass
   175	  exact avgOver_nonneg _ _ fun xy => outcome_event_weight_nonneg S xy.1 xy.2 _
   176	
   177	/-- Value at least `1 - ε` implies total rejection mass at most `ε`. -/
   178	theorem total_rejection_mass_le (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
   179	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) : totalRejectionMass S ≤ ε := by
   180	  rw [total_rejection_mass_eq_one_sub_value]
   181	  linarith
   182	
   183	/-- Conditioned rejection mass is nonnegative. -/
   184	theorem rejection_mass_nonneg (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType) :
   185	    0 ≤ rejectionMass S x y :=
   186	  outcome_event_weight_nonneg S x y fun a b => msWinPredicate x y a b = false
   187	
   188	/-- A supported conditioned rejection mass is at most 36 times total rejection. -/
   189	theorem rejection_mass_le_thirty_six_mul_total (S : Strategy msGame)
   190	    {xy : MsType × MsType}
   191	    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :
   192	    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 ≤ 36 * totalRejectionMass S := by
   193	  have hrejection : 0 ≤ rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 :=
   194	    rejection_mass_nonneg S xy.1 xy.2
   195	  have hweight := ms_question_weight_ge hxy
   196	  have hterm :
   197	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy *
   198	          rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 ≤ totalRejectionMass S := by
   199	    unfold totalRejectionMass avgOver
   200	    exact Finset.single_le_sum
   201	      (fun z _ => mul_nonneg
   202	        ((graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).nonnegative z)
   203	        (rejection_mass_nonneg S z.1 z.2)) hxy
   204	  have hscaled : (1 / 36 : ℝ) * rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 ≤
   205	      (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).weight xy *
   206	        rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 :=
   207	    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hweight hrejection
   208	  nlinarith
   209	
   210	/-- A supported conditioned rejection mass is at most `36 * ε`. -/
   211	theorem rejection_mass_le (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
   212	    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) {xy : MsType × MsType}
   213	    (hxy : xy ∈ (graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty).support) :
   214	    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 ≤ 36 * ε := by
   215	  calc
   216	    rejectionMass S xy.1 xy.2 ≤ 36 * totalRejectionMass S :=
   217	      rejection_mass_le_thirty_six_mul_total S hxy
   218	    _ ≤ 36 * ε :=
   219	      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (total_rejection_mass_le S ε hwin) (by norm_num)
   220	
   221	/-- An event which always rejects has mass at most the conditioned rejection mass. -/
   222	theorem outcome_event_weight_le_rejection_mass (S : Strategy msGame) (x y : MsType)
   223	    (E : MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Prop) [DecidableRel E]
   224	    (hE : ∀ a b, E a b → msWinPredicate x y a b = false) :
   225	    outcomeEventWeight S x y E ≤ rejectionMass S x y := by
   226	  exact outcome_event_weight_mono S x y E _ hE

   228	/-! ## Malformed answers and cell consistency -/
   229	
   230	/-- The selected constraint bit, with a wrong-form single-bit answer folded to zero. -/
   231	def constraintBitOrZero (k : Fin 3) : MsAnswer → ZMod 2
   232	  | .triple β => β k
   233	  | .bit _ => 0
   234	
   235	/-- Whether an answer has the wrong form for a variable question. -/
   236	def wrongVariableAnswer : MsAnswer → Bool
   237	  | .triple _ => true
   238	  | .bit _ => false
   239	
   240	/-- Whether an answer has the wrong form for a constraint question. -/
   241	def wrongConstraintAnswer : MsAnswer → Bool
   242	  | .triple _ => false
   243	  | .bit _ => true
   244	
   245	/-- The three cells in any fixed row or column are distinct. -/
   246	theorem constraint_vars_injective (i : Fin 6) : Function.Injective (msConstraintVars i) := by
   247	  intro k l hkl
   248	  apply Fin.ext
   249	  unfold msConstraintVars at hkl
   250	  split at hkl <;> simp only [Fin.mk.injEq] at hkl ⊢ <;> omega
   251	
   252	/-- Every Magic Square variable is incident to a row constraint. -/
   253	theorem every_variable_is_incident (j : Fin 9) :
   254	    ∃ i : Fin 6, ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j := by
   255	  let i : Fin 6 := ⟨j.val / 3, by omega⟩
   256	  let k : Fin 3 := ⟨j.val % 3, Nat.mod_lt _ (by omega)⟩
   257	  refine ⟨i, k, ?_⟩
   258	  apply Fin.ext
   259	  simp only [msConstraintVars, i, k]
   260	  rw [if_pos (by omega)]

     6

     8	decision predicate, packages the game as a `SymmetricGame`, and defines the
     9	observable associated with a binary measurement.
    10	
    11	## References

    29	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`. -/

     4	/-!
     5	# Binary observables and the state-dependent distance
     6	
     7	This file collects the notions in which the quantum linearity theorem of
     8	Natarajan and Vidick is stated: binary observables, the rank-one density
     9	operator of an ancillary vector, and the squared state-dependent distance
    10	between two operators weighted by a positive semidefinite trace-one operator.
    11	The theorem itself, `exists_exactly_linear_observables`, is stated and proved
    12	in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity.lean` from the Boolean Fourier,
    13	operator BLR, Naimark rounding, and representation stability modules under
    14	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/`, all of which build on this file.
    15	
    16	## Main definitions
    17	
    18	* `IsBinaryObservable`: a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity,
    19	  together with its algebra: the identity is a binary observable, so is the
    20	  product of two commuting ones, every binary observable is an isometry, and it
    21	  remains one after ampliation by the identity of another tensor factor.
    22	* `ancProj`: the rank-one density operator `|v⟩⟨v|` of a vector `v`.
    23	* `stateDepDistSq`: the squared state-dependent distance
    24	  `d_ρ(S, T)^2 = Re Tr((S - T)^† (S - T) ρ)`.
    25	
    26	## References
    27	
    28	The notions are those of `thm:linearity` in
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`, quoted in the QPBT
    30	paper at `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`
    31	from Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574,
    32	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1088`; the state-dependent distance is
    33	defined there at lines 866--875.
    34	-/
    35	
    36	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    37	
    38	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    39	
    40	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    41	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    42	
    43	noncomputable section
    44	
    45	/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    46	This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    47	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`, quoted at paper
    48	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
    49	def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    50	    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
    51	  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1
    52	
    53	namespace IsBinaryObservable
    54	
    55	variable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {X Y : Op ι}
    56	
    57	/-- A binary observable is self-adjoint. -/
    58	theorem conjTranspose_eq (hX : IsBinaryObservable X) : Xᴴ = X := hX.1
    59	
    60	/-- A binary observable squares to the identity. -/
    61	theorem mul_self_eq_one (hX : IsBinaryObservable X) : X * X = 1 := hX.2
    62	
    63	/-- A binary observable is isometric: being self-adjoint and an involution, its
    64	adjoint is its own inverse. -/
    65	theorem isometry (hX : IsBinaryObservable X) : Xᴴ * X = 1 := by
    66	  rw [hX.conjTranspose_eq, hX.mul_self_eq_one]
    67	
    68	/-- The identity is a binary observable. -/
    69	theorem one : IsBinaryObservable (1 : Op ι) :=
    70	  ⟨Matrix.isHermitian_one, one_mul 1⟩
    71	
    72	/-- The product of two commuting binary observables is a binary observable. -/
    73	theorem mul (hX : IsBinaryObservable X) (hY : IsBinaryObservable Y)
    74	    (hcomm : X * Y = Y * X) : IsBinaryObservable (X * Y) := by
    75	  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    76	  · rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hX.conjTranspose_eq,
    77	      hY.conjTranspose_eq, ← hcomm]
    78	  · calc X * Y * (X * Y) = X * (Y * X) * Y := by noncomm_ring
    79	      _ = X * (X * Y) * Y := by rw [hcomm]
    80	      _ = X * X * (Y * Y) := by noncomm_ring
    81	      _ = 1 := by rw [hX.mul_self_eq_one, hY.mul_self_eq_one, one_mul]
    82	
    83	end IsBinaryObservable
    84	
    85	/-- The ampliation `O ⊗ 1` of a binary observable by the identity of a second
    86	tensor factor is a binary observable.  This is the sense in which the original
    87	observables `A(a)` act on the extended space in display (8) of
    88	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1083-1086`; it is also the way a Magic Square
    89	observable of one player acts on the joint space of `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
    90	theorem isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    91	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] {O : Op ι} (hO : IsBinaryObservable O) :
    92	    IsBinaryObservable (heteroKron O (1 : Op ι')) := by
    93	  unfold heteroKron
    94	  simp only [Matrix.kronecker]
    95	  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    96	  · rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker, hO.conjTranspose_eq,
    97	      Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
    98	  · rw [← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul, hO.mul_self_eq_one, Matrix.one_mul,
    99	      Matrix.one_kronecker_one]
   100	
   101	/-- The ampliation `1 ⊗ O` of a binary observable by the identity of the first
   102	tensor factor is a binary observable; this is the mirror of
   103	`isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one` for the second player's factor in
   104	`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   105	theorem isBinaryObservable_one_heteroKron {ι ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   106	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] {O : Op ι'} (hO : IsBinaryObservable O) :
   107	    IsBinaryObservable (heteroKron (1 : Op ι) O) := by
   108	  unfold heteroKron
   109	  simp only [Matrix.kronecker]
   110	  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   111	  · rw [Matrix.IsHermitian, Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker, hO.conjTranspose_eq,
   112	      Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
   113	  · rw [← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul, hO.mul_self_eq_one, Matrix.one_mul,
   114	      Matrix.one_kronecker_one]
   115	
   116	/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector.  This
   117	is the state `|anc⟩⟨anc|` of the extension `ρ' = ρ ⊗ |anc⟩⟨anc|` in
   118	`thm:linearity`, blueprint
   119	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`. -/
   120	noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   121	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
   122	  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v
   123	  Matrix.vecMulVec w (star w)
   124	
   125	/-- Squared state-dependent distance between two operators.  This is the
   126	quantity `d_ρ(S,T)^2` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
   127	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:104-150`, the state-dependent
   128	distance of `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`. -/
   129	noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   130	    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
   131	  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re
   132	
   133	end
   134	
   135	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
