    fix(review): faithful closeness convention for the rigidity chain (PR 162 round 2)
    
    F1: delete the pass-through abbreviation `IsReflection`; its explanatory
    prose becomes the `## Reflections` section comment, which keeps pointing
    readers at `MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable`.
    
    F2: the state-dependent relation of `Rigidity/Reflections.lean` bounds the
    unsquared norm, while `M ~_delta N` of `thm:ms-rigidity` (blueprint
    `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:249`, paper
    `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:644-646`) bounds the squared
    quantity. Rename `CloseOn` to `NormCloseOn`, state in its docstring and in
    the module docstring what it is and what it is not, and add the explicit
    conversion `NormCloseOn.opDistSq_le` into `opDistSq`, the formal counterpart
    of the source's relation (`def:povm-distance`). The anticommutation
    docstrings no longer claim to be the source's relation, and
    `msVarObsA_anticommute_opDistSq` / `msVarObsB_anticommute_opDistSq` record
    the source's own form at the printed scale `sqrt eps` for `eps <= 1`. No
    paper-labelled statement is weakened: the norm bound `624 * sqrt eps` gives
    the squared bound `624 ^ 2 * eps`, which is stronger than the printed
    `O(sqrt eps)` in that range.
    
    F3: `NormCloseOn.neg`, `NormCloseOn.smul` and `NormCloseOn.mul_left_subst`
    move from `Rigidity/Anticommutation.lean` and `Rigidity/CellRelations.lean`
    to the module that defines the relation.
    
    F4: delete `isProj_heteroKron` and use the imported
    `MakingMeasurementsProjective.isProj_kronecker`.

references/cs-paper/introduction.tex:1:In \cite{peres1990incompatible,mermin1990simple}, Mermin and Peres discovered an algebraic coincidence related to the $3\times3$ ``Magic Square'' of operators on $\C^2\otimes \C^2$ in Figure \ref{fig:magic-square-operators-introduction}.
references/cs-paper/introduction.tex:3:If we pick any row and take the product of the three operators in that row (note that they commute, so the order does not matter), we get the identity operator. Similarly, we can try this with the columns. Two of the columns give identity while the other  gives $-1$ times identity. Thus, the product of these nine operators depends on whether they are multiplied row by row or column by column. This can be exploited to define a two-player, one-referee game called the Mermin--Peres Magic Square game \cite{aravind2004quantum} (see Definition \ref{definition:linear-constraint-game} and Figure \ref{fig:magic-square-equations} for a formal definition). Informally, the Mermin--Peres Magic Square game mod $2$ is as follows. The players claim to have a $3\times 3$ square of numbers in which each row and each of the first two columns sums to $0\pmod 2$, while the third column sums to $1\pmod 2$. (The players are usually called ``provers'', since they try to prove that they have such a square.) The referee asks the first player to present a row of the supposed square and the second to present a column. They reply respectively with the $3$ entries of that row and column in $\{0,1\}$. They win if their responses sum to $0$ or $1$ as appropriate, and they give the same number for the entry where the row and column overlap. This game can be won with probability $1$ by provers that share two pairs of maximally entangled qubits of dimension $2$, but provers with no entanglement can win with probability at most $\frac89$. Games which are won in the classical case with probability $< 1$ but are won in the quantum case with probability $1$ are known as \emph{pseudotelepathy games}.

references/cs-paper/self-testing.tex:3:In this section, we introduce our main robust self-testing theorem for linear constraint system games with solution groups of a certain form. In \S \ref{subsection:exact-self-testing}, to ease understanding, we start by stating and proving an exact version of the theorem. In \S \ref{subsection:state-dependent-distance} through \S \ref{subsection:quant-stabilizer-state-bounds}, we introduce the necessary tools to prove an approximate version of the self-testing theorem. \S \ref{subsection:state-dependent-distance} introduces the state-dependent distance and some of its properties. \S \ref{subsection:stability-lemma} proves a stability lemma for representations of finite groups, which allows us to deduce that the action of a strategy winning with high probability is close to the action of a representation of the solution group.  \S \ref{subsection:quant-van-kampen} presents a quantitative version of the van Kampen Lemma from Section \S \ref{subsection:van-kampen-diagrams}, which is key in bounding the robustness of the main theorem. \S \ref{subsection:quant-stabilizer-state-bounds} shows that if a joint state is approximately stabilized by the action of the Pauli group on two tensor factors, then it is close to the maximally entangled state on the two tensor factors. In \S \ref{subsection:robust-self-testing} we combine these tools to prove our robust self-testing theorem.

references/cs-paper/conclusion.tex:1:We have presented a general robust self-testing theorem for a certain class of linear constraint system games, using the group-theoretic approach of Cleve, Liu and Slofstra. We specialized this theorem to the cases of the Magic Square and Magic Pentagram games mod $2$, obtaining robust self-testing theorems for respectively two and three pairs of maximally entangled qubits and the associated ideal measurements. Furthermore, we applied our theorem to a certain $n$-fold product of these games to obtain a robust self-testing theorem for a tensor product of $n$ maximally entangled qubits and the associated $n$-qubit Pauli measurements. The following are some remaining open questions.

references/cs-paper/Arxiv v2 - Robust LCS self testing/introduction.tex:1:In \cite{peres1990incompatible,mermin1990simple}, Mermin and Peres discovered an algebraic coincidence related to the $3\times3$ ``Magic Square'' of operators on $\C^2\otimes \C^2$ in Figure \ref{fig:magic-square-operators-introduction}.
references/cs-paper/Arxiv v2 - Robust LCS self testing/introduction.tex:3:If we pick any row and take the product of the three operators in that row (note that they commute, so the order does not matter), we get the identity operator. Similarly, we can try this with the columns. Two of the columns give identity while the other  gives $-1$ times identity. Thus, the product of these nine operators depends on whether they are multiplied row by row or column by column. This can be exploited to define a two-player, one-referee game called the Mermin--Peres Magic Square game \cite{aravind2004quantum} (see Definition \ref{definition:linear-constraint-game} and Figure \ref{fig:magic-square-equations} for a formal definition). Informally, the Mermin--Peres Magic Square game mod $2$ is as follows. The players claim to have a $3\times 3$ square of numbers in which each row and each of the first two columns sums to $0\pmod 2$, while the third column sums to $1\pmod 2$. (The players are usually called ``provers'', since they try to prove that they have such a square.) The referee asks the first player to present a row of the supposed square and the second to present a column. They reply respectively with the $3$ entries of that row and column in $\{0,1\}$. They win if their responses sum to $0$ or $1$ as appropriate, and they give the same number for the entry where the row and column overlap. This game can be won with probability $1$ by provers that share two pairs of maximally entangled qubits of dimension $2$, but provers with no entanglement can win with probability at most $\frac89$. Games which are won in the classical case with probability $< 1$ but are won in the quantum case with probability $1$ are known as \emph{pseudotelepathy games}.

references/cs-paper/Arxiv v2 - Robust LCS self testing/introduction.tex:32:In order to answer questions like this, Cleve, Liu, and Slofstra \cite{cleve2016perfect} associate to each LCS game an algebraic invariant called the \emph{solution group} (see Section \ref{sec:linear-constraint-games} for a precise definition), and they relate the winnability of the game to the representation theory of the group. In particular, they show that any quantum strategy winning the game with probability $1$ corresponds to a representation of the solution group---in other words, that the observables in a winning strategy must satisfy the algebraic relations captured by the group. This reduces the problem of finding LCS games with interesting properties to the problem of finding finitely-presented groups with analogous representation-theoretic properties, while maintaining combinatorial control over their presentations. Slofstra used this idea together with techniques from combinatorial group theory to resolve the weak Tsirelson problem \cite{slofstra2016tsirelson}. By including some techniques from the stability theory of group representations, he improved this result to show that the set of quantum correlations is not closed \cite{slofstra2017set}. In words, he constructed an LCS game which can be won with probability arbitrarily close to $1$ with finite-dimensional quantum strategies, but cannot be won with probability $1$ by any finite (or infinite) dimensional quantum strategy (in the tensor product model).

references/cs-paper/Arxiv v2 - Robust LCS self testing/introduction.tex:39:This question was resolved by Wu et.\ al \cite{wu2016device}. They showed that any operators satisfying the same algebraic relations as those in the Magic Square game are equivalent to those in Figure \ref{fig:magic-square-operators-introduction}, up to local isometry and tensoring with identity. This is sometimes referred to as \emph{rigidity} of the Magic Square game. Moreover, they showed that the Magic Square game is \emph{robustly rigid}, or \emph{robustly self-testing}. Informally, we say that a game is \emph{rigid with $O(\d(\e))$-robustness and perfect completeness} if whenever Alice and Bob win the game with probability at least $1-\e$, then there is a local isometry taking their state and measurement operators $O(\d(\e))$-close to an ideal strategy, possibly tensored with identity.
references/cs-paper/Arxiv v2 - Robust LCS self testing/introduction.tex:44:Our main result is a robust self-testing theorem which applies to any linear constraint game with sufficiently nice solution group; this is stated as Theorem \ref{thm:robust-self-testing}. Our proof employs the machinery of \cite{cleve2016perfect} and \cite{slofstra2016tsirelson}. We apply the general self-testing result to conclude robust rigidity for the Magic Square game, the Magic Pentagram game, and for a certain repeated product of these two games. We informally state these results now. We emphasize that these results are not new, but it is new that we can achieve all three as simple corollaries of the main self-testing machinery. The general result holds for LCS games mod $d$, but the only nontrivial application we have is for LCS games mod $2$.

references/cs-paper/Arxiv v2 - Robust LCS self testing/self-testing.tex:3:In this section, we introduce our main robust self-testing theorem for linear constraint system games with solution groups of a certain form. In \S \ref{subsection:state-dependent-distance} through \S \ref{subsection:quant-stabilizer-state-bounds}, we introduce the necessary tools to prove an approximate version of the self-testing theorem. \S \ref{subsection:state-dependent-distance} introduces the state-dependent distance and some of its properties. \S \ref{subsection:stability-lemma} proves a stability lemma for representations of finite groups, which allows us to deduce that the action of a strategy winning with high probability is close to the action of a representation of the solution group.  \S \ref{subsection:quant-van-kampen} presents a quantitative version of the van Kampen Lemma from Section \S \ref{subsection:van-kampen-diagrams}, which is key in bounding the robustness of the main theorem. \S \ref{subsection:quant-stabilizer-state-bounds} shows that if a joint state is approximately stabilized by the action of the Pauli group on two tensor factors, then it is close to the maximally entangled state on the two tensor factors. In \S \ref{subsection:robust-self-testing} we combine these tools to prove our robust self-testing theorem.

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.MagicSquareTheorems.Rigidity.CellRelations
+
+/-!
+# Approximate anticommutation in the Magic Square game
+
+The Magic Square is the smallest linear constraint system whose solution group
+forces two of its generators to anticommute.  This file carries out that
+computation on the projective dilation of an arbitrary strategy, in the
+state-dependent norm and with explicit constants.
+
+The computation proceeds in three identical steps.  Each step takes two
+constraints sharing exactly one cell and rewrites a product of two cell
+reflections, one from each constraint, as the signed product of the two
+reflections at the remaining cells.  Iterating the step around the grid returns
+to the pair one started from, in the opposite order and with the sign reversed
+by the exceptional parity of the third column; this yields the approximate
+anticommutation of the two reflections at the cells labelled by the paper's
+first and fifth variables.
+
+## References
+
+The statement supported here is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
+proved in Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9; the argument
+below is the Magic Square instance of the solution-group computation used there
+(their Figure describing the generators of the solution group).  The variable
+and constraint indices are zero-based, so the paper's first and fifth variables
+are the cells `0` and `4`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-! ## Placement of an operator on one player's tensor factor -/
+
+/-- Formalization-only: an operator acting on Alice's tensor factor alone. -/
+private def AlicePlaced {ιA ιB : Type} [DecidableEq ιB] (Z : Op (ιA × ιB)) : Prop :=
+  ∃ M : Op ιA, Z = heteroKron M 1
+
+/-- Formalization-only: an operator acting on Bob's tensor factor alone. -/
+private def BobPlaced {ιA ιB : Type} [DecidableEq ιA] (Z : Op (ιA × ιB)) : Prop :=
+  ∃ N : Op ιB, Z = heteroKron 1 N
+
+/-- Formalization-only: operators of the two players commute. -/
+private theorem AlicePlaced.comm {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
+    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] {Z W : Op (ιA × ιB)} (hZ : AlicePlaced Z)
+    (hW : BobPlaced W) : Z * W = W * Z := by
+  obtain ⟨M, rfl⟩ := hZ
+  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := hW
+  exact heteroKron_comm M N
+
+/-- Formalization-only: products stay on Alice's tensor factor. -/
+private theorem AlicePlaced.mul {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA]
+    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] {Z W : Op (ιA × ιB)} (hZ : AlicePlaced Z)
+    (hW : AlicePlaced W) : AlicePlaced (Z * W) := by
+  obtain ⟨M, rfl⟩ := hZ
+  obtain ⟨M', rfl⟩ := hW
+  exact ⟨M * M', by rw [heteroKron_mul, mul_one]⟩
+
+/-- Formalization-only: products stay on Bob's tensor factor. -/
+private theorem BobPlaced.mul {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
+    [Fintype ιB] {Z W : Op (ιA × ιB)} (hZ : BobPlaced Z)
+    (hW : BobPlaced W) : BobPlaced (Z * W) := by
+  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := hZ
+  obtain ⟨N', rfl⟩ := hW
+  exact ⟨N * N', by rw [heteroKron_mul, mul_one]⟩
+
+/-- Formalization-only: scalar multiples stay on Bob's tensor factor. -/
+private theorem BobPlaced.smul {ιA ιB : Type} [DecidableEq ιA] {c : ℂ} {Z : Op (ιA × ιB)}
+    (hZ : BobPlaced Z) : BobPlaced (c • Z) := by
+  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := hZ
+  exact ⟨c • N, (heteroKron_smul_right c 1 N).symm⟩
+
+/-- Formalization-only: operators of the two players commute. -/
+private theorem BobPlaced.comm {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
+    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] {Z W : Op (ιA × ιB)} (hZ : BobPlaced Z)
+    (hW : AlicePlaced W) : Z * W = W * Z := (hW.comm hZ).symm
+
+/-- Formalization-only: scalar multiples stay on Alice's tensor factor. -/
+private theorem AlicePlaced.smul {ιA ιB : Type} [DecidableEq ιB] {c : ℂ}
+    {Z : Op (ιA × ιB)} (hZ : AlicePlaced Z) : AlicePlaced (c • Z) := by
+  obtain ⟨M, rfl⟩ := hZ
+  exact ⟨c • M, (heteroKron_smul_left c M 1).symm⟩
+
+/-- Alice's cell reflection acts on her tensor factor alone. -/
+private theorem alicePlaced_msCellObsA (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
+    AlicePlaced (msCellObsA S i k) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
+
+/-- Bob's variable reflection acts on his tensor factor alone. -/
+private theorem bobPlaced_msVarObsB (S : Strategy msGame) (j : Fin 9) :
+    BobPlaced (msVarObsB S j) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
+
+/-- Alice's variable reflection acts on her tensor factor alone. -/
+private theorem alicePlaced_msVarObsA (S : Strategy msGame) (j : Fin 9) :
+    AlicePlaced (msVarObsA S j) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
+
+/-- Bob's cell reflection acts on his tensor factor alone. -/
+private theorem bobPlaced_msCellObsB (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3) :
+    BobPlaced (msCellObsB S i k) := ⟨_, rfl⟩
+
+/-! ## Isometry bookkeeping -/
+
+/-- Formalization-only: a product of isometric operators is isometric. -/
+private theorem isometry_mul_isometry {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    {U V : Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) (hV : Vᴴ * V = 1) : (U * V)ᴴ * (U * V) = 1 := by
+  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul]
+  calc Vᴴ * Uᴴ * (U * V) = Vᴴ * (Uᴴ * U) * V := by noncomm_ring
+    _ = 1 := by rw [hU, mul_one, hV]
+
+/-- Formalization-only: a unit scalar multiple of an isometric operator is
+isometric. -/
+private theorem isometry_smul {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {c : ℂ}
+    (hstar : star c = c) (hsq : c * c = 1) {U : Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) :
+    (c • U)ᴴ * (c • U) = 1 := by
+  have hstarT : (c • U)ᴴ = c • Uᴴ := by
+    rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, star_smul, Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, hstar]
+  rw [hstarT, Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_smul, smul_smul, hU, hsq, one_smul]
+
+/-- The complex sign of a binary value is fixed by conjugation. -/
+theorem star_bitSign_ofReal (c : ZMod 2) :
+    star ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) = ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
+  simp
+
+/-! ## One step of the solution-group computation -/
+
+/-- One step of the Magic Square solution-group computation.  Here `X`, `Y`, `W`
+are three reflections of one player attached to a single constraint, with `X`
+and `W` commuting and `Y` close to the signed product `sI • (X * W)` prescribed
+by that constraint; the reflections `P`, `Q`, `R` play the same role for a
+second constraint with sign `sJ`.  The reflections `Pa` and `Ra` are the
+counterparts of `P` and `R` on the other player, and `P` is close to `X` because
+the two constraints share the cell that `X` and `P` are attached to.  The
+conclusion rewrites the product `Y * Q` as the signed product of the two
+remaining reflections.  Formalization-only support for `thm:ms-rigidity`,
+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
+private theorem normCloseOn_step {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
+    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)} {δ : ℝ}
+    {X Y W P Q R Pa Ra : Op (ιA × ιB)} {sI sJ : ℂ}
+    (hXr : IsBinaryObservable X) (hYr : IsBinaryObservable Y) (hWr : IsBinaryObservable W)
+    (hPr : IsBinaryObservable P)
+    (hPar : IsBinaryObservable Pa) (hRar : IsBinaryObservable Ra)
+    (hcY : Y * (Ra * Pa) = (Ra * Pa) * Y)
+    (hcXW : (X * W) * (Ra * Pa) = (Ra * Pa) * (X * W))
+    (hcP : P * Ra = Ra * P) (hcX : X * Ra = Ra * X)
+    (hXW : X * W = W * X)
+    (hsJnorm : ‖sJ‖ = 1) (hsIstar : star sI = sI) (hsIsq : sI * sI = 1)
+    (hQ : NormCloseOn ψ δ Q (sJ • (P * R)))
+    (hY : NormCloseOn ψ δ Y (sI • (X * W)))
+    (hPPa : NormCloseOn ψ δ P Pa) (hRRa : NormCloseOn ψ δ R Ra)
+    (hPX : NormCloseOn ψ (δ + δ) P X) :
+    NormCloseOn ψ (10 * δ) (Y * Q) ((sI * sJ) • (W * R)) := by
+  have hPRa : NormCloseOn ψ (δ + δ) (P * R) (Ra * Pa) := by
+    have s1 : NormCloseOn ψ δ (P * R) (P * Ra) := NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hPr.isometry hRRa
+    rw [show P * Ra = Ra * P from hcP] at s1
+    exact s1.trans (NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hRar.isometry hPPa)
+  have hRaPa : (Ra * Pa)ᴴ * (Ra * Pa) = 1 :=
+    isometry_mul_isometry hRar.isometry hPar.isometry
+  have hXWiso : (X * W)ᴴ * (X * W) = 1 := isometry_mul_isometry hXr.isometry hWr.isometry
+  have hsXWiso : (sI • (X * W))ᴴ * (sI • (X * W)) = 1 :=
+    isometry_smul hsIstar hsIsq hXWiso
+  have hcsXW : (sI • (X * W)) * (Ra * Pa) = (Ra * Pa) * (sI • (X * W)) := by
+    rw [Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_smul, hcXW]
+  have h2 : NormCloseOn ψ (δ + δ + δ + (δ + δ)) (Y * (P * R)) ((sI • (X * W)) * (P * R)) :=
+    NormCloseOn.mul_left_subst hY hPRa hYr.isometry hsXWiso hRaPa hcY hcsXW
+  have hPRXR : NormCloseOn ψ (δ + (δ + δ) + δ) (P * R) (X * R) :=
+    NormCloseOn.mul_left_subst hPX hRRa hPr.isometry hXr.isometry hRar.isometry hcP hcX
+  have h3 : NormCloseOn ψ (δ + (δ + δ) + δ)
+      ((sI • (X * W)) * (P * R)) ((sI • (X * W)) * (X * R)) :=
+    NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hsXWiso hPRXR
+  have e2 : (sI • (X * W)) * (X * R) = sI • (W * R) := by
+    rw [Matrix.smul_mul]
+    congr 1
+    calc (X * W) * (X * R) = X * (W * X) * R := by noncomm_ring
+      _ = X * (X * W) * R := by rw [hXW]
+      _ = (X * X) * (W * R) := by noncomm_ring
+      _ = W * R := by rw [hXr.mul_self_eq_one, one_mul]
+  have hA : NormCloseOn ψ δ (Y * Q) (sJ • (Y * (P * R))) := by
+    have h1 : NormCloseOn ψ δ (Y * Q) (Y * (sJ • (P * R))) :=
+      NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hYr.isometry hQ
+    rwa [Matrix.mul_smul] at h1
+  have hB := NormCloseOn.smul hsJnorm h2
+  have hC := NormCloseOn.smul hsJnorm h3
+  have e3 : sJ • ((sI • (X * W)) * (X * R)) = (sI * sJ) • (W * R) := by
+    rw [e2, smul_smul, mul_comm]
+  have hfinal := (hA.trans hB).trans hC
+  rw [e3] at hfinal
+  exact hfinal.mono (by linarith)
+
+/-! ## Negation and the sign of a constraint -/
+
+/-- Formalization-only: closeness to a negative is symmetric in the two
+operators. -/
+private theorem normCloseOn_neg_swap {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι} {δ : ℝ} {M N : Op ι} (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M (-N)) :
+    NormCloseOn ψ δ N (-M) := by
+  change ‖applyOperatorToState (N - -M) ψ‖ ≤ δ
+  rw [show N - -M = M - -N by abel]
+  exact h
+
+/-! ## The Magic Square instance of one step -/
+
+/-- One step of the solution-group computation for Bob's cell reflections: for
+two constraints sharing the cell at positions `k₀` and `l₀`, the product of the
+reflections at the positions `k₁` and `l₁` is close to the signed product of the
+reflections at the two remaining positions. -/
+theorem msCellObsB_step (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
+    (I J : Fin 6) (k₀ k₁ k₂ l₀ l₁ l₂ : Fin 3)
+    (hI : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero k₀ a + constraintBitOrZero k₁ a +
+      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a)
+    (hJ : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero l₀ a + constraintBitOrZero l₁ a +
+      constraintBitOrZero l₂ a = constraintBitSum a)
+    (hcell : msConstraintVars I k₀ = msConstraintVars J l₀) :
+    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (10 * (12 * Real.sqrt ε))
+      (msCellObsB S I k₁ * msCellObsB S J l₁)
+      ((((bitSign (msParity I) : ℝ) : ℂ) * ((bitSign (msParity J) : ℝ) : ℂ)) •
+        (msCellObsB S I k₂ * msCellObsB S J l₂)) :=
+  normCloseOn_step (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S I k₀) (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S I k₁)
+    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S I k₂) (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S J l₀)
+    (isBinaryObservable_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l₀))
+    (isBinaryObservable_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l₂))
+    (((alicePlaced_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l₂)).mul
+      (alicePlaced_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l₀))).comm
+      (bobPlaced_msCellObsB S I k₁)).symm
+    (((alicePlaced_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l₂)).mul
+      (alicePlaced_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l₀))).comm
+      ((bobPlaced_msCellObsB S I k₀).mul (bobPlaced_msCellObsB S I k₂))).symm
+    ((alicePlaced_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l₂)).comm
+      (bobPlaced_msCellObsB S J l₀)).symm
+    ((alicePlaced_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J l₂)).comm
+      (bobPlaced_msCellObsB S I k₀)).symm
+    (msCellObsB_comm S I k₀ k₂) (norm_bitSign_ofReal (msParity J))
+    (star_bitSign_ofReal (msParity I)) (bitSign_ofReal_mul_self (msParity I))
+    (msCellObsB_single_close S ε hwin J l₀ l₁ l₂ hJ)
+    (msCellObsB_single_close S ε hwin I k₀ k₁ k₂ hI)
+    (msVarObsA_close_msCellObsB S ε hwin J l₀).symm
+    (msVarObsA_close_msCellObsB S ε hwin J l₂).symm
+    (msCellObsB_close_of_same_cell S ε hwin J I l₀ k₀ hcell.symm)
+
+/-- Replacing both factors of a product of two of Bob's cell reflections by the
+reflections that other constraints attach to the same two cells. -/
+theorem msCellObsB_mul_close_of_same_cells (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
+    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) (I J I' J' : Fin 6) (k l k' l' : Fin 3)
+    (h1 : msConstraintVars I k = msConstraintVars I' k')
+    (h2 : msConstraintVars J l = msConstraintVars J' l') :
+    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (6 * (12 * Real.sqrt ε))
+      (msCellObsB S I k * msCellObsB S J l)
+      (msCellObsB S I' k' * msCellObsB S J' l') := by
+  have hright := NormCloseOn.isometry_mul (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S I k).isometry
+    (msCellObsB_close_of_same_cell S ε hwin J J' l l' h2)
+  have hleft := NormCloseOn.mul_left_subst
+    (msCellObsB_close_of_same_cell S ε hwin I I' k k' h1)
+    (msVarObsA_close_msCellObsB S ε hwin J' l').symm
+    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S I k).isometry
+    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsB S I' k').isometry
+    (isBinaryObservable_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J' l')).isometry
+    ((alicePlaced_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J' l')).comm
+      (bobPlaced_msCellObsB S I k)).symm
+    ((alicePlaced_msVarObsA S (msConstraintVars J' l')).comm
+      (bobPlaced_msCellObsB S I' k')).symm
+  exact (hright.trans hleft).mono (by linarith)
+
+/-! ## Approximate anticommutation of the two logical Pauli pairs -/
+
+/-- The two reflections that Alice attaches to the cells of the paper's first
+and fifth variables approximately anticommute on the dilated state, in the
+unsquared state-dependent norm and at the scale `624 * sqrt ε`.  The source
+states this conclusion for the squared distance: the last display of
+`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:244-249`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:640-646`, reads
+`⟨ψ|(M - N)ᴴ (M - N)|ψ⟩ ≤ O(sqrt ε)`; that form is
+`msVarObsA_anticommute_opDistSq` below, obtained from this bound through
+`NormCloseOn.opDistSq_le`. -/
+theorem msVarObsA_anticommute (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) :
+    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (624 * Real.sqrt ε)
+      (msVarObsA S 0 * msVarObsA S 4) (-(msVarObsA S 4 * msVarObsA S 0)) := by
+  have hA : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 1 a + constraintBitOrZero 0 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 2 a = constraintBitSum a := by
+    intro a; simp only [constraintBitSum]; ring
+  have hA' : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 0 a + constraintBitOrZero 1 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 2 a = constraintBitSum a := fun a => rfl
+  have hB : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 2 a + constraintBitOrZero 0 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 1 a = constraintBitSum a := by
+    intro a; simp only [constraintBitSum]; ring
+  have hB' : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 2 a + constraintBitOrZero 1 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 0 a = constraintBitSum a := by
+    intro a; simp only [constraintBitSum]; ring
+  have hC : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 0 a + constraintBitOrZero 2 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 1 a = constraintBitSum a := by
+    intro a; simp only [constraintBitSum]; ring
+  have hC' : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 1 a + constraintBitOrZero 2 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 0 a = constraintBitSum a := by
+    intro a; simp only [constraintBitSum]; ring
+  have hsign_pos : ∀ i : Fin 6, i ≠ 5 →
+      ((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) = 1 := by
+    intro i hi
+    have hp : msParity i = 0 := by
+      unfold msParity

+/-- Alice's half of the last conclusion of `thm:ms-rigidity` in the convention
+of the source.  The relation `M ≈_δ N` of blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:249`

+bound of `msVarObsA_anticommute` gives that statement with the explicit constant
+`624 ^ 2`; the same estimate gives the bound `624 ^ 2 * ε`, which is stronger in
+this range. -/
+theorem msVarObsA_anticommute_opDistSq (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
+    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) (hε : ε ≤ 1) :
+    opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ => msVarObsA S 0 * msVarObsA S 4)
+        (fun _ => -(msVarObsA S 4 * msVarObsA S 0))
+        (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ ≤ 624 ^ 2 * Real.sqrt ε := by
+  refine (msVarObsA_anticommute S ε hwin).opDistSq_le.trans ?_
+  have h1 : Real.sqrt ε ≤ 1 := Real.sqrt_le_one.mpr hε
+  have h0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt ε := Real.sqrt_nonneg ε
+  nlinarith [mul_nonneg h0 (sub_nonneg.mpr h1)]

+/-! ## The computation on Alice's cell reflections -/

+/-- One of Alice's three cell reflections of a constraint question is close, on
+the dilated state, to the signed product of the other two. -/
+theorem msCellObsA_single_close (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
+    (i : Fin 6) (k₀ k₁ k₂ : Fin 3)
+    (hsum : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero k₀ a + constraintBitOrZero k₁ a +
+      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a) :
+    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) (msCellObsA S i k₁)
+      (((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) •
+        (msCellObsA S i k₀ * msCellObsA S i k₂)) := by
+  have hprod := msCellObsA_prod_close_of S ε hwin i k₀ k₁ k₂ hsum
+  have hX2 : msCellObsA S i k₀ * msCellObsA S i k₀ = 1 :=
+    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S i k₀).mul_self_eq_one
+  have hZ2 : msCellObsA S i k₂ * msCellObsA S i k₂ = 1 :=
+    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S i k₂).mul_self_eq_one
+  have hZY : msCellObsA S i k₂ * msCellObsA S i k₁ =
+      msCellObsA S i k₁ * msCellObsA S i k₂ := msCellObsA_comm S i k₂ k₁
+  have hZX : msCellObsA S i k₂ * msCellObsA S i k₀ =
+      msCellObsA S i k₀ * msCellObsA S i k₂ := msCellObsA_comm S i k₂ k₀
+  have hU : (msCellObsA S i k₂ * msCellObsA S i k₀)ᴴ *
+      (msCellObsA S i k₂ * msCellObsA S i k₀) = 1 :=
+    ((isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S i k₂).mul
+      (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S i k₀) hZX).isometry
+  have e1 : (msCellObsA S i k₂ * msCellObsA S i k₀) *
+      (msCellObsA S i k₀ * msCellObsA S i k₁ * msCellObsA S i k₂) =
+      msCellObsA S i k₁ := by
+    calc (msCellObsA S i k₂ * msCellObsA S i k₀) *
+          (msCellObsA S i k₀ * msCellObsA S i k₁ * msCellObsA S i k₂)
+        = msCellObsA S i k₂ *
+            ((msCellObsA S i k₀ * msCellObsA S i k₀) * msCellObsA S i k₁) *
+            msCellObsA S i k₂ := by noncomm_ring
+      _ = msCellObsA S i k₂ * msCellObsA S i k₁ * msCellObsA S i k₂ := by
+          rw [hX2, one_mul]
+      _ = msCellObsA S i k₁ * msCellObsA S i k₂ * msCellObsA S i k₂ := by rw [hZY]
+      _ = msCellObsA S i k₁ := by rw [mul_assoc, hZ2, mul_one]
+  have e2 : (msCellObsA S i k₂ * msCellObsA S i k₀) *
+      (((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op _)) =
+      ((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • (msCellObsA S i k₀ * msCellObsA S i k₂) := by
+    rw [Matrix.mul_smul, mul_one, hZX]
+  have h := NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hU hprod
+  rw [e1, e2] at h
+  exact h
+
+/-- A product of two of Alice's cell reflections is close, on the dilated state,
+to the product of Bob's variable reflections at the same two cells, taken in the
+reverse order. -/
+theorem msCellObsA_mul_close (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
+    (I J : Fin 6) (k l : Fin 3) :
+    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε + 12 * Real.sqrt ε)
+      (msCellObsA S I k * msCellObsA S J l)
+      (msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l) * msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars I k)) := by
+  have h1 : NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε)
+      (msCellObsA S I k * msCellObsA S J l)
+      (msCellObsA S I k * msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l)) :=
+    NormCloseOn.isometry_mul (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S I k).isometry
+      (msCellObsA_close_msVarObsB S ε hwin J l)
+  rw [show msCellObsA S I k * msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l) =
+      msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l) * msCellObsA S I k from
+    msCellObsA_comm_msVarObsB S I k (msConstraintVars J l)] at h1
+  exact h1.trans (NormCloseOn.isometry_mul (isBinaryObservable_msVarObsB S _).isometry
+    (msCellObsA_close_msVarObsB S ε hwin I k))
+
+/-- Two of Alice's cell reflections attached to a common cell by two different
+constraint questions are close on the dilated state. -/
+theorem msCellObsA_close_of_same_cell (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
+    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) (I J : Fin 6) (k l : Fin 3)
+    (hcell : msConstraintVars I k = msConstraintVars J l) :
+    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε + 12 * Real.sqrt ε)
+      (msCellObsA S I k) (msCellObsA S J l) := by
+  have p1 : NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) (msCellObsA S I k)
+      (msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars I k)) := msCellObsA_close_msVarObsB S ε hwin I k
+  have p2 : NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε)
+      (msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l)) (msCellObsA S J l) :=
+    (msCellObsA_close_msVarObsB S ε hwin J l).symm
+  rw [hcell] at p1
+  exact p1.trans p2
+
+/-- One step of the solution-group computation for Alice's cell reflections. -/
+theorem msCellObsA_step (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
+    (I J : Fin 6) (k₀ k₁ k₂ l₀ l₁ l₂ : Fin 3)
+    (hI : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero k₀ a + constraintBitOrZero k₁ a +
+      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a)
+    (hJ : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero l₀ a + constraintBitOrZero l₁ a +
+      constraintBitOrZero l₂ a = constraintBitSum a)
+    (hcell : msConstraintVars I k₀ = msConstraintVars J l₀) :
+    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (10 * (12 * Real.sqrt ε))
+      (msCellObsA S I k₁ * msCellObsA S J l₁)
+      ((((bitSign (msParity I) : ℝ) : ℂ) * ((bitSign (msParity J) : ℝ) : ℂ)) •
+        (msCellObsA S I k₂ * msCellObsA S J l₂)) :=
+  normCloseOn_step (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S I k₀) (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S I k₁)
+    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S I k₂) (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S J l₀)
+    (isBinaryObservable_msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l₀))
+    (isBinaryObservable_msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l₂))
+    (((bobPlaced_msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l₂)).mul
+      (bobPlaced_msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l₀))).comm
+      (alicePlaced_msCellObsA S I k₁)).symm
+    (((bobPlaced_msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l₂)).mul
+      (bobPlaced_msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l₀))).comm
+      ((alicePlaced_msCellObsA S I k₀).mul (alicePlaced_msCellObsA S I k₂))).symm
+    ((bobPlaced_msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l₂)).comm
+      (alicePlaced_msCellObsA S J l₀)).symm
+    ((bobPlaced_msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J l₂)).comm
+      (alicePlaced_msCellObsA S I k₀)).symm
+    (msCellObsA_comm S I k₀ k₂) (norm_bitSign_ofReal (msParity J))
+    (star_bitSign_ofReal (msParity I)) (bitSign_ofReal_mul_self (msParity I))
+    (msCellObsA_single_close S ε hwin J l₀ l₁ l₂ hJ)
+    (msCellObsA_single_close S ε hwin I k₀ k₁ k₂ hI)
+    (msCellObsA_close_msVarObsB S ε hwin J l₀)
+    (msCellObsA_close_msVarObsB S ε hwin J l₂)
+    (msCellObsA_close_of_same_cell S ε hwin J I l₀ k₀ hcell.symm)
+
+/-- Replacing both factors of a product of two of Alice's cell reflections by
+the reflections that other constraints attach to the same two cells. -/
+theorem msCellObsA_mul_close_of_same_cells (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
+    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) (I J I' J' : Fin 6) (k l k' l' : Fin 3)
+    (h1 : msConstraintVars I k = msConstraintVars I' k')
+    (h2 : msConstraintVars J l = msConstraintVars J' l') :
+    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (6 * (12 * Real.sqrt ε))
+      (msCellObsA S I k * msCellObsA S J l)
+      (msCellObsA S I' k' * msCellObsA S J' l') := by
+  have hright := NormCloseOn.isometry_mul (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S I k).isometry
+    (msCellObsA_close_of_same_cell S ε hwin J J' l l' h2)
+  have hleft := NormCloseOn.mul_left_subst
+    (msCellObsA_close_of_same_cell S ε hwin I I' k k' h1)

+    (isBinaryObservable_msCellObsA S I' k').isometry
+    (isBinaryObservable_msVarObsB S (msConstraintVars J' l')).isometry
+    (msCellObsA_comm_msVarObsB S I k (msConstraintVars J' l'))
+    (msCellObsA_comm_msVarObsB S I' k' (msConstraintVars J' l'))

+/-- The two reflections that Bob attaches to the cells of the paper's first and
+fifth variables approximately anticommute on the dilated state, in the unsquared
+state-dependent norm and at the scale `624 * sqrt ε`.  The source states the
+second half of the last conclusion of `thm:ms-rigidity` for the squared
+distance: blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:244-249`, paper
+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:640-646`, reads
+`⟨ψ|(M - N)ᴴ (M - N)|ψ⟩ ≤ O(sqrt ε)`; that form is
+`msVarObsB_anticommute_opDistSq` below, obtained from this bound through
+`NormCloseOn.opDistSq_le`. -/

+    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (624 * Real.sqrt ε)
+      (msVarObsB S 0 * msVarObsB S 4) (-(msVarObsB S 4 * msVarObsB S 0)) := by
+  have hA : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 1 a + constraintBitOrZero 0 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 2 a = constraintBitSum a := by
+    intro a; simp only [constraintBitSum]; ring
+  have hA' : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 0 a + constraintBitOrZero 1 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 2 a = constraintBitSum a := fun a => rfl
+  have hB : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 2 a + constraintBitOrZero 0 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 1 a = constraintBitSum a := by
+    intro a; simp only [constraintBitSum]; ring
+  have hB' : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 2 a + constraintBitOrZero 1 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 0 a = constraintBitSum a := by
+    intro a; simp only [constraintBitSum]; ring
+  have hC : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 0 a + constraintBitOrZero 2 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 1 a = constraintBitSum a := by
+    intro a; simp only [constraintBitSum]; ring
+  have hC' : ∀ a : MsAnswer, constraintBitOrZero 1 a + constraintBitOrZero 2 a +
+      constraintBitOrZero 0 a = constraintBitSum a := by
+    intro a; simp only [constraintBitSum]; ring
+  have hsign_pos : ∀ i : Fin 6, i ≠ 5 → ((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) = 1 := by
+    intro i hi
+    have hp : msParity i = 0 := by
+      unfold msParity
+      rw [if_neg]
+      intro hv
+      exact hi (Fin.ext hv)
+    rw [hp]
+    norm_num [bitSign]
+  have hsign_neg : ((bitSign (msParity 5) : ℝ) : ℂ) = -1 := by
+    have hp : msParity 5 = 1 := by norm_num [msParity]
+    rw [hp]
+    norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one]
+  have stepA := msCellObsA_step S ε hwin 0 4 1 0 2 0 1 2 hA hA' (by decide)
+  rw [hsign_pos 0 (by decide), hsign_pos 4 (by decide), one_mul, one_smul] at stepA
+  have stepB := msCellObsA_step S ε hwin 5 2 2 0 1 2 1 0 hB hB' (by decide)
+  rw [hsign_neg, hsign_pos 2 (by decide), mul_one, neg_one_smul] at stepB
+  have stepC := msCellObsA_step S ε hwin 1 3 0 2 1 1 2 0 hC hC' (by decide)
+  rw [hsign_pos 1 (by decide), hsign_pos 3 (by decide), one_mul, one_smul] at stepC
+  have linkA := msCellObsA_mul_close_of_same_cells S ε hwin 0 4 5 2 2 2 0 1
+    (by decide) (by decide)
+  have linkB := msCellObsA_mul_close_of_same_cells S ε hwin 5 2 1 3 1 0 2 2
+    (by decide) (by decide)
+  have linkC := msCellObsA_mul_close_of_same_cells S ε hwin 1 3 4 0 1 0 1 0
+    (by decide) (by decide)
+  have hstart := (msCellObsA_mul_close S ε hwin 0 4 0 1).symm
+  have hend := msCellObsA_mul_close S ε hwin 4 0 1 0
+  rw [show msConstraintVars 4 1 = 4 from by decide,
+    show msConstraintVars 0 0 = 0 from by decide] at hstart hend
+  have hchain := ((((((hstart.trans stepA).trans linkA).trans stepB).trans
+    linkB.neg).trans stepC.neg).trans linkC.neg).trans hend.neg
+  exact normCloseOn_neg_swap (hchain.mono (by linarith))
+
+/-- Bob's half of the last conclusion of `thm:ms-rigidity` in the convention of
+the source.  The relation `M ≈_δ N` of blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:249` and
+paper `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:644-646` bounds
+`⟨ψ|(M - N)ᴴ (M - N)|ψ⟩`, formalized by `opDistSq` (`def:povm-distance`), and
+the anticommutation is printed at the scale `sqrt ε`.  For `ε ≤ 1` the norm
+bound of `msVarObsB_anticommute` gives that statement with the explicit constant
+`624 ^ 2`; the same estimate gives the bound `624 ^ 2 * ε`, which is stronger in
+this range. -/
+theorem msVarObsB_anticommute_opDistSq (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ)
+    (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value) (hε : ε ≤ 1) :
+    opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ => msVarObsB S 0 * msVarObsB S 4)
+        (fun _ => -(msVarObsB S 4 * msVarObsB S 0))
+        (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ ≤ 624 ^ 2 * Real.sqrt ε := by
+  refine (msVarObsB_anticommute S ε hwin).opDistSq_le.trans ?_
+  have h1 : Real.sqrt ε ≤ 1 := Real.sqrt_le_one.mpr hε
+  have h0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt ε := Real.sqrt_nonneg ε
+  nlinarith [mul_nonneg h0 (sub_nonneg.mpr h1)]
+
+end

     4	/-!
     5	# A simultaneous projective dilation of a Magic Square strategy
     6	
     7	The rigidity argument for the Magic Square game is stated for an arbitrary
     8	tensor-product strategy, whose measurements are positive operator valued
     9	measures.  The self-testing argument, however, manipulates projections.  This
    10	file removes that discrepancy by dilating an arbitrary strategy to a projective
    11	one without changing any observable quantity.
    12	
    13	Each local Hilbert space `ℂ^ι` is enlarged by one auxiliary register whose
    14	basis is indexed by `Option MsAnswer`, and the original space is identified with
    15	the *ground slice* `ℂ^ι ⊗ |⊥⟩`.  The one-measurement Naimark lemma of the low
    16	individual degree development supplies, for every question separately, a family
    17	of projections on the enlarged space whose compression to the ground slice
    18	returns the original effects; the ancilla is the same for all questions, so the
    19	identification of `ℂ^ι` with the ground slice is a single isometry serving every
    20	question at once.  Folding the deficiency `1 - ∑_a P_a` into one distinguished
    21	answer turns the dilated family into a complete projective measurement without
    22	disturbing the compression, because the original effects already sum to the
    23	identity.
    24	
    25	Since the dilated state is the image of the original state under the two ground
    26	embeddings, every Born probability, and hence the game value and all the
    27	rejection, malformed-answer, cell-consistency and parity masses of the
    28	value-to-parity layer, is unchanged.  Conversely, the local isometries produced
    29	by a rigidity argument applied to the dilated strategy compose with the ground
    30	embeddings to give local isometries of the original strategy, and the
    31	state-dependent norms occurring in the conclusion of `thm:ms-rigidity` transfer
    32	along that composition.
    33	
    34	## References
    35	
    36	The rigidity statement supported here is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
    37	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
    39	proved in Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.  The dilation reuses the
    40	one-measurement Naimark lemma of

    54	/-! ## Orthogonality inside a subnormalized family of projections -/
    55	
    56	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
    57	(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  If an orthogonal projection `P` and a
    58	positive semidefinite operator `Q` satisfy `P + Q ≤ 1`, then `P` annihilates
    59	`Q`.  Indeed `Tr(P Q)` is nonnegative because both operators are positive
    60	semidefinite, while `0 ≤ Tr(P (1 - P - Q)) = -Tr(P Q)` because `1 - P - Q` is
    61	positive semidefinite and `P` is idempotent; so the pairing vanishes and the
    62	product of two positive semidefinite operators with vanishing trace pairing is
    63	zero. -/
    64	theorem mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_of_add_le_one {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    65	    {P Q : Op d} (hP : IsProj P) (hQ : 0 ≤ Q) (hPQ : P + Q ≤ 1) :
    66	    P * Q = 0 := by
    67	  have hrest : (0 : Op d) ≤ 1 - (P + Q) := sub_nonneg.mpr hPQ
    68	  have hexpand : P * (1 - (P + Q)) = -(P * Q) := by
    69	    have hPP : P * P = P := hP.isIdempotentElem
    70	    rw [Matrix.mul_sub, Matrix.mul_add, hPP, Matrix.mul_one]
    71	    abel
    72	  have hle : Complex.re (Matrix.trace (P * Q)) ≤ 0 := by
    73	    have h := trace_mul_nonneg_of_nonneg hP.nonneg hrest
    74	    rw [hexpand] at h
    75	    simpa using h
    76	  have hge : 0 ≤ Complex.re (Matrix.trace (P * Q)) :=
    77	    trace_mul_nonneg_of_nonneg hP.nonneg hQ
    78	  exact mul_eq_zero_of_nonneg_of_trace_mul_eq_zero hP.nonneg hQ (le_antisymm hle hge)
    79	
    80	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
    81	(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  A finite family of orthogonal
    82	projections whose sum is at most the identity is mutually orthogonal: for two
    83	distinct indices the two projections already sum to at most the identity, so the
    84	previous lemma applies. -/
    85	theorem mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family {d α : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    86	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {P : α → Op d} (hP : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
    87	    (hsum : ∑ a, P a ≤ 1) {a b : α} (hab : a ≠ b) :
    88	    P a * P b = 0 := by
    89	  refine mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_of_add_le_one (hP a) (hP b).nonneg ?_
    90	  refine le_trans ?_ hsum
    91	  have hpair : ∑ c ∈ ({a, b} : Finset α), P c = P a + P b := by
    92	    rw [Finset.sum_pair hab]
    93	  rw [← hpair]
    94	  exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
    95	    (fun c _ _ => (hP c).nonneg)
    96	
    97	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`
    98	(blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`).  The sum of a mutually orthogonal
    99	family of projections is again an orthogonal projection; mutual orthogonality is
   100	supplied by the hypothesis that the sum is at most the identity. -/
   101	theorem isProj_sum_of_isProj_of_sum_le_one {d α : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   102	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {P : α → Op d} (hP : ∀ a, IsProj (P a))
   103	    (hsum : ∑ a, P a ≤ 1) :
   104	    IsProj (∑ a, P a) := by
   105	  constructor
   106	  · show (∑ a, P a) * (∑ a, P a) = ∑ a, P a
   107	    rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   108	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   109	    rw [Matrix.mul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single a]
   110	    · exact (hP a).isIdempotentElem
   111	    · exact fun b _ hba => mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family hP hsum (Ne.symm hba)
   112	    · intro ha
   113	      exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a) ha
   114	  · show star (∑ a, P a) = ∑ a, P a
   115	    rw [star_sum]
   116	    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => (hP a).isSelfAdjoint

   118	/-! ## The ground slice of an enlarged local space -/
   119	
   120	/-- The linear map sending a vector `x` of `ℂ^ι` to `x ⊗ |⊥⟩`, where `|⊥⟩` is the
   121	basis vector of the auxiliary register `ℂ^{Option α}` indexed by the adjoined
   122	point.  Formalization-only support for the dilation used by `thm:ms-rigidity`,
   123	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   124	def naimarkEmbeddingMap (ι α : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   125	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
   126	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × Option α) where
   127	  toFun x := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ι × Option α) ℂ).symm
   128	    (fun p => if p.2 = none then x p.1 else 0)
   129	  map_add' x y := by
   130	    ext p
   131	    by_cases h : p.2 = none <;> simp [h]
   132	  map_smul' c x := by
   133	    ext p
   134	    by_cases h : p.2 = none <;> simp [h]
   135	
   136	/-- The isometric identification of a local Hilbert space `ℂ^ι` with the *ground
   137	slice* `ℂ^ι ⊗ |⊥⟩` of the enlarged space `ℂ^{ι × Option α}`.  This single
   138	embedding serves every question of the dilation supporting `thm:ms-rigidity`,
   139	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
   140	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
   141	noncomputable def naimarkEmbedding (ι α : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   142	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
   143	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × Option α) :=
   144	  LinearMap.isometryOfInner (naimarkEmbeddingMap ι α) <| by
   145	    intro x y
   146	    simp [PiLp.inner_apply, Fintype.sum_prod_type, naimarkEmbeddingMap]
   147	
   148	/-- The coordinates of the ground embedding: the amplitude is carried to the
   149	auxiliary basis vector `|⊥⟩` and vanishes on the other auxiliary vectors. -/
   150	@[simp]
   151	theorem naimarkEmbedding_apply {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   152	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (p : ι × Option α) :
   153	    naimarkEmbedding ι α x p = if p.2 = none then x p.1 else 0 := rfl
   154	
   155	/-- The compression of an operator on the enlarged space to the ground slice.
   156	Formalization-only support for the dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   157	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   158	def naimarkCompression {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   159	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op (ι × Option α)) : Op ι :=
   160	  M.submatrix (fun i => (i, none)) (fun j => (j, none))
   161	
   162	/-- The entries of the ground-slice compression. -/
   163	@[simp]
   164	theorem naimarkCompression_apply {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   165	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op (ι × Option α)) (i j : ι) :
   166	    naimarkCompression (α := α) M i j = M (i, none) (j, none) := rfl
   167	
   168	/-- The compression of the zero operator to the ground slice vanishes. -/
   169	@[simp]
   170	theorem naimarkCompression_zero {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   171	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
   172	    naimarkCompression (α := α) (0 : Op (ι × Option α)) = 0 := by
   173	  ext i j; simp
   174	
   175	/-- The compression to the ground slice is additive. -/
   176	theorem naimarkCompression_add {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   177	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M N : Op (ι × Option α)) :
   178	    naimarkCompression (α := α) (M + N) =
   179	      naimarkCompression (α := α) M + naimarkCompression (α := α) N := by
   180	  ext i j; simp
   181	
   182	/-- The compression to the ground slice commutes with finite sums. -/
   183	theorem naimarkCompression_sum {ι α β : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   184	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] (M : β → Op (ι × Option α)) :
   185	    naimarkCompression (α := α) (∑ b, M b) = ∑ b, naimarkCompression (α := α) (M b) := by
   186	  ext i j; simp [Matrix.sum_apply]
   187	
   188	/-- The compression of the identity to the ground slice is the identity. -/
   189	@[simp]
   190	theorem naimarkCompression_one {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   191	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
   192	    naimarkCompression (α := α) (1 : Op (ι × Option α)) = 1 := by
   193	  ext i j
   194	  by_cases h : i = j <;> simp [Matrix.one_apply, h]
   195	
   196	/-- The operator on the enlarged space that acts as `M` on the ground slice and
   197	annihilates its orthogonal complement.  Formalization-only support for the
   198	dilation of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   199	def naimarkInflation {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   200	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op ι) : Op (ι × Option α) :=
   201	  Matrix.of fun p q => if p.2 = none ∧ q.2 = none then M p.1 q.1 else 0
   202	
   203	/-- The entries of the inflation of an operator to the enlarged space. -/
   204	@[simp]
   205	theorem naimarkInflation_apply {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   206	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op ι) (p q : ι × Option α) :
   207	    naimarkInflation (α := α) M p q =
   208	      if p.2 = none ∧ q.2 = none then M p.1 q.1 else 0 := rfl
   209	
   210	/-- Inflating an operator to the enlarged space and compressing it back returns
   211	the original operator. -/
   212	@[simp]
   213	theorem naimarkCompression_naimarkInflation {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   214	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M : Op ι) :
   215	    naimarkCompression (α := α) (naimarkInflation (α := α) M) = M := by
   216	  ext i j; simp
   217	
   218	/-- The compression to the ground slice respects differences. -/
   219	theorem naimarkCompression_sub {ι α : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   220	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (M N : Op (ι × Option α)) :
   221	    naimarkCompression (α := α) (M - N) =
   222	      naimarkCompression (α := α) M - naimarkCompression (α := α) N := by
   223	  ext i j; simp

   225	/-! ## The dilated projective measurement -/
   226	
   227	/-- A one-measurement Naimark dilation of a positive operator valued measure,
   228	chosen once and for all.  It provides orthogonal projections on the enlarged
   229	space `ℂ^{d × Option α}` whose ground-slice compressions are the given effects;
   230	see `references/ldt-paper/orthonormalization.tex:121-159`. -/
   231	noncomputable def naimarkData {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   232	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) : OneMeasNaimarkData α d :=
   233	  Classical.choose (oneMeasNaimark M.toSubmeasurement)
   234	
   235	/-- The chosen dilation dilates the intended measurement. -/
   236	theorem naimarkData_source {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   237	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
   238	    (naimarkData M).source = M.toSubmeasurement :=
   239	  Classical.choose_spec (oneMeasNaimark M.toSubmeasurement)
   240	
   241	/-- The dilated projections indexed by genuine answers already sum to at most the
   242	identity, since the projection attached to the adjoined point is positive
   243	semidefinite. -/
   244	theorem naimarkData_sum_some_le_one {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   245	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
   246	    ∑ a : α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some a) ≤ 1 := by
   247	  have hsplit : ∑ oa : Option α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect oa =
   248	      (naimarkData M).liftedEffect none +
   249	        ∑ a : α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some a) :=
   250	    Fintype.sum_option (f := fun oa => (naimarkData M).liftedEffect oa)
   251	  have hle := (naimarkData M).lifted_sum_le_one
   252	  rw [hsplit] at hle
   253	  have hnone : (0 : Op (d × Option α)) ≤ (naimarkData M).liftedEffect none :=
   254	    (naimarkData M).lifted_pos none
   255	  exact le_trans (le_add_of_nonneg_left hnone) hle
   256	
   257	/-- The sum of the dilated projections indexed by genuine answers is itself an
   258	orthogonal projection. -/
   259	theorem naimarkData_isProj_sum_some {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   260	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
   261	    IsProj (∑ a : α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some a)) :=
   262	  isProj_sum_of_isProj_of_sum_le_one
   263	    (fun a => (naimarkData M).lifted_isProj (some a))
   264	    (naimarkData_sum_some_le_one M)
   265	
   266	/-- The effects of the dilated measurement.  The projection attached to the
   267	answer `a` is the Naimark projection of `a`, except that the distinguished answer
   268	`a₀` also absorbs the deficiency `1 - ∑_a P_a`, which makes the family complete.
   269	Formalization-only construction supporting `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   270	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   271	noncomputable def naimarkDilatedEffect {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   272	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (a₀ a : α) :
   273	    Op (d × Option α) :=
   274	  (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some a) +
   275	    (if a = a₀ then 1 - ∑ b : α, (naimarkData M).liftedEffect (some b) else 0)
   276	
   277	/-- The dilated effects are positive semidefinite. -/
   278	theorem naimarkDilatedEffect_pos {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   279	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (a₀ a : α) :
   280	    0 ≤ naimarkDilatedEffect M a₀ a := by

   444	/-! ## The dilated Magic Square strategy -/
   445	
   446	/-- The projective dilation of an arbitrary Magic Square strategy.  Both local
   447	spaces acquire one auxiliary register indexed by `Option MsAnswer`, the state is
   448	carried to the ground slice, and each question measurement is replaced by its
   449	Naimark dilation, the deficiency being absorbed by the answer `bit 0`.  This is
   450	the projective strategy on which the self-testing argument of `thm:ms-rigidity`
   451	operates; blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
   452	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
   453	noncomputable def msDilatedStrategy (S : Strategy msGame) : Strategy msGame where
   454	  ιA := S.ιA × Option MsAnswer
   455	  ιB := S.ιB × Option MsAnswer
   456	  ψ := naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ
   457	  ψ_norm := by
   458	    show ‖naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ‖ = 1
   459	    rw [naimarkDilatedState_norm]
   460	    exact S.ψ_norm
   461	  A x := naimarkDilatedMeasurement (α := MsAnswer) (S.A x) (MsAnswer.bit 0)
   462	  B y := naimarkDilatedMeasurement (α := MsAnswer) (S.B y) (MsAnswer.bit 0)

   464	/-- The state of the dilated strategy is the image of the original state under
   465	the two ground embeddings. -/

   467	theorem msDilatedStrategy_psi (S : Strategy msGame) :
   468	    (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ = naimarkDilatedState MsAnswer S.ψ := rfl

   470	/-- Alice's dilated question measurements are the Naimark dilations of her
   471	original ones. -/

   474	    ((msDilatedStrategy S).A x).effect a =
   475	      naimarkDilatedEffect (α := MsAnswer) (S.A x) (MsAnswer.bit 0) a := rfl
   476	
   477	/-- Bob's dilated question measurements are the Naimark dilations of his
   478	original ones. -/
   479	@[simp]
   480	theorem msDilatedStrategy_B_effect (S : Strategy msGame) (y : MsType) (b : MsAnswer) :
   481	    ((msDilatedStrategy S).B y).effect b =

   486	theorem msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A (S : Strategy msGame) (x : MsType) :
   487	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective ((msDilatedStrategy S).A x) :=
   488	  naimarkDilatedMeasurement_isProjective (α := MsAnswer) (S.A x) (MsAnswer.bit 0)

    10	carrier is needed here.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, from
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    24	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 207-222, paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    26	-/
    27	inductive MsType where
    28	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    29	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    30	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    31	
    32	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    33	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    34	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    35	-/
    36	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    37	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    38	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    39	
    40	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    41	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`; paper
    42	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    43	-/
    44	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    45	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    46	
    47	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    48	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    50	-/
    51	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    52	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    53	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    54	
    55	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    56	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    57	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`,
    58	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    59	-/
    60	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    61	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    62	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    63	
    64	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    65	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`,
    66	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    67	-/
    68	inductive MsAnswer where
    69	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    70	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    71	  deriving DecidableEq
    72	
    73	/-- A formalization-only total relabeling from the global Magic Square answer
    74	alphabet to a bit. It folds wrong-form answers into zero so that a variable
    75	question yields a complete binary measurement. -/
    76	def msBitOrZero : MsAnswer → ZMod 2
    77	  | .bit b => b
    78	  | .triple _ => 0
    79	
    80	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    81	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    82	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    84	-/
    85	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    86	
    87	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    88	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    89	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    91	-/
    92	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    93	  toFun
    94	    | .triple β => .inl β
    95	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    96	  invFun
    97	    | .inl β => .triple β
    98	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    99	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   100	  right_inv := by
   101	    intro x
   102	    cases x <;> rfl
   103	
   104	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
   105	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
   106	
   107	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
   108	
   109	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   110	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 207-222; paper
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   112	-/
   113	def msWinPredicate :
   114	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   115	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   116	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   117	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   118	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   119	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   120	      decide
   121	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   122	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   123	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   124	      decide
   125	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   126	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   127	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   128	
   129	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   130	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:207-222`, paper origin
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   132	-/
   133	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   134	  QuestionA := MsType
   135	  QuestionB := MsType
   136	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   137	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   138	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   139	  μ_prob := by
   140	    apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   141	    refine ⟨(.constraint 0, .var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
   142	    simp [msEdges]
   143	  decide := msWinPredicate
   144	
   145	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# The Magic Square cell relations on the dilated strategy
     5	
     6	Every question of the projectively dilated Magic Square strategy carries a
     7	complete projective measurement, so each binary relabelling of its answers
     8	produces a reflection.  Three reflections are attached to a constraint question,
     9	one for each cell of the row or column, and one reflection is attached to each
    10	variable question; the three reflections of a constraint commute exactly and
    11	their product, in any order, is the reflection of the sum of the three reported
    12	bits.  Reflections of the two players commute exactly.
    13	
    14	The value-to-parity relations are converted here into operator estimates on the
    15	dilated state, with explicit constants: the six row and column products are
    16	close to the sign prescribed by the corresponding linear equation, and the two
    17	reflections that the two players attach to a common cell are close to each
    18	other.  The two logical Pauli pairs are the reflections at the cells labelled by
    19	the paper's first and fifth variables.
    20	
    21	## References
    22	
    23	The statement supported here is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
    24	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, from
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
    26	proved in Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9.  The variable and
    27	constraint indices are zero-based, so the paper's first and fifth variables are
    28	the cells `0` and `4`.
    29	-/

    41	/-- The sign of a binary value is `1` or `-1`. -/
    42	theorem bit_sign_eq_one_or_neg_one (b : ZMod 2) : bitSign b = 1 ∨ bitSign b = -1 := by
    43	  rcases (by decide : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x = 0 ∨ x = 1) b with h | h <;> rw [h]
    44	  · left
    45	    norm_num [bitSign]
    46	  · right
    47	    norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one]
    48	
    49	/-- The sign is injective on binary values. -/
    50	theorem bit_sign_injective : Function.Injective bitSign := by
    51	  intro b c hbc
    52	  by_contra hne
    53	  rcases (by decide : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x = 0 ∨ x = 1) b with hb | hb <;>
    54	    rcases (by decide : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x = 0 ∨ x = 1) c with hc | hc
    55	  · exact hne (hb.trans hc.symm)
    56	  · rw [hb, hc] at hbc
    57	    norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one] at hbc
    58	  · rw [hb, hc] at hbc
    59	    norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one] at hbc
    60	  · exact hne (hb.trans hc.symm)

    66	/-- Two sign observables of the two players, placed on the composite space,
    67	differ in the state-dependent norm by at most twice the square root of the Born
    68	mass of the answer pairs on which the two labels disagree.  This is the estimate
    69	that turns every mass of the value-to-parity layer into an operator relation of
    70	`thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
    71	theorem norm_alice_sub_bob_signObs_sq_le (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
    72	    (y : G.QuestionB) (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.A x))
    73	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.B y))
    74	    (f : G.AnswerA → ZMod 2) (g : G.AnswerB → ZMod 2) :
    75	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (signObs (T.A x) f) 1 -
    76	        heteroKron 1 (signObs (T.B y) g)) T.ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
    77	      4 * outcomeEventWeight T x y (fun a b => f a ≠ g b) := by
    78	  classical
    79	  have hAone : (1 : Op T.ιA) = ∑ a, (1 : ℂ) • (T.A x).effect a := by
    80	    simpa using smul_one_eq_sum_smul_effect (T.A x) (1 : ℂ)
    81	  have hBone : (1 : Op T.ιB) = ∑ b, (1 : ℂ) • (T.B y).effect b := by
    82	    simpa using smul_one_eq_sum_smul_effect (T.B y) (1 : ℂ)
    83	  have hexpand : heteroKron (signObs (T.A x) f) 1 - heteroKron 1 (signObs (T.B y) g) =
    84	      ∑ a, ∑ b, ((bitSign (f a) - bitSign (g b) : ℝ) : ℂ) •
    85	        heteroKron ((T.A x).effect a) ((T.B y).effect b) := by
    86	    rw [signObs, signObs]
    87	    nth_rewrite 1 [hBone]
    88	    nth_rewrite 1 [hAone]
    89	    rw [joint_expand, joint_expand, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    90	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
    91	    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    92	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
    93	    rw [← sub_smul]
    94	    congr 1
    95	    push_cast
    96	    ring
    97	  rw [hexpand]
    98	  refine norm_apply_joint_defect_sq_le T x y hA hB
    99	    (fun a b => bitSign (f a) - bitSign (g b)) (fun a b => f a ≠ g b) ?_ ?_
   100	  · intro a b
   101	    rcases bit_sign_eq_one_or_neg_one (f a) with h1 | h1 <;>
   102	      rcases bit_sign_eq_one_or_neg_one (g b) with h2 | h2 <;>
   103	        simp only [h1, h2] <;> norm_num
   104	  · intro a b hab
   105	    rw [not_not] at hab
   106	    rw [hab, sub_self]

   108	/-- Alice's sign observable deviates from a constant sign by at most twice the
   109	square root of the mass of the answers carrying the other label. -/
   110	theorem norm_alice_signObs_sub_const_sq_le (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   111	    (y : G.QuestionB) (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.A x))
   112	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.B y))
   113	    (f : G.AnswerA → ZMod 2) (c : ZMod 2) :
   114	    ‖applyOperatorToState (heteroKron (signObs (T.A x) f) 1 -
   115	        ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op (T.ιA × T.ιB))) T.ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
   116	      4 * aliceEventWeight T x (fun a => f a ≠ c) := by
   117	  classical
   118	  have hconst : heteroKron (1 : Op T.ιA) (signObs (T.B y) (fun _ => c)) =
   119	      ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op (T.ιA × T.ιB)) := by
   120	    rw [signObs, ← smul_one_eq_sum_smul_effect (T.B y) (((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ)),
   121	      heteroKron_smul_right, heteroKron_one_one]
   122	  have h := norm_alice_sub_bob_signObs_sq_le T x y hA hB f (fun _ => c)
   123	  rw [hconst] at h
   124	  refine le_trans h (le_of_eq ?_)
   125	  congr 1
   126	  exact outcome_event_weight_left_eq T x y (fun a => f a ≠ c)
   127	
   128	/-- Bob's sign observable deviates from a constant sign by at most twice the
   129	square root of the mass of the answers carrying the other label. -/
   130	theorem norm_bob_signObs_sub_const_sq_le (T : Strategy G) (x : G.QuestionA)
   131	    (y : G.QuestionB) (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.A x))
   132	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (T.B y))
   133	    (g : G.AnswerB → ZMod 2) (c : ZMod 2) :
   134	    ‖applyOperatorToState (((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op (T.ιA × T.ιB)) -
   135	        heteroKron 1 (signObs (T.B y) g)) T.ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
   136	      4 * bobEventWeight T y (fun b => c ≠ g b) := by
   137	  classical
   138	  have hconst : heteroKron (signObs (T.A x) (fun _ => c)) (1 : Op T.ιB) =
   139	      ((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Op (T.ιA × T.ιB)) := by
   140	    rw [signObs, ← smul_one_eq_sum_smul_effect (T.A x) (((bitSign c : ℝ) : ℂ)),
   141	      heteroKron_smul_left, heteroKron_one_one]
   142	  have h := norm_alice_sub_bob_signObs_sq_le T x y hA hB (fun _ => c) g
   143	  rw [hconst] at h
   144	  refine le_trans h (le_of_eq ?_)
   145	  congr 1
   146	  exact outcome_event_weight_right_eq T x y (fun b => c ≠ g b)

   150	/-! ## Comparison of Born masses with the game error -/
   151	
   152	/-- Formalization-only: a squared state-dependent bound by four times a mass
   153	which is itself bounded by `36 * ε` yields closeness at scale `12 * sqrt ε`. -/
   154	private theorem normCloseOn_of_sq_le {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   155	    {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι} {M N : Op ι} {m ε : ℝ}
   156	    (hsq : ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤ 4 * m) (hm0 : 0 ≤ m)
   157	    (hm : m ≤ 36 * ε) : NormCloseOn ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) M N := by
   158	  have hε : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ε := by
   159	    have h36 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 36 * ε := le_trans hm0 hm
   160	    linarith
   161	  have hbound : ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤ (12 * Real.sqrt ε) ^ 2 := by
   162	    have hsq' : (12 * Real.sqrt ε) ^ 2 = 144 * ε := by
   163	      rw [mul_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hε]
   164	      ring
   165	    rw [hsq']
   166	    linarith
   167	  calc ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖
   168	      = Real.sqrt (‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ^ 2) :=
   169	        (Real.sqrt_sq (norm_nonneg _)).symm
   170	    _ ≤ Real.sqrt ((12 * Real.sqrt ε) ^ 2) := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hbound
   171	    _ = 12 * Real.sqrt ε := Real.sqrt_sq (by positivity)

   295	/-- The sum of the three answer bits reported for a constraint question, with
   296	malformed answers contributing zero. -/
   297	def constraintBitSum (a : MsAnswer) : ZMod 2 :=
   298	  constraintBitOrZero 0 a + constraintBitOrZero 1 a + constraintBitOrZero 2 a
   299	
   300	/-- An answer whose three reported bits do not sum to the prescribed parity is a
   301	parity failure in the sense of the value-to-parity layer. -/
   302	theorem constraintParityFailure_of_bitSum_ne (i : Fin 6) (a : MsAnswer)
   303	    (h : constraintBitSum a ≠ msParity i) : ConstraintParityFailure i a := by
   304	  cases a with
   305	  | bit γ => exact wrong_constraint_answer_implies_parity_failure i (MsAnswer.bit γ) rfl
   306	  | triple β =>
   307	      intro hprod
   308	      apply h
   309	      have hsum : bitSign (∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = bitSign (msParity i) := by
   310	        rw [bit_sign_sum_fin_three]
   311	        exact hprod
   312	      have hbit := bit_sign_injective hsum
   313	      rw [Fin.sum_univ_three] at hbit
   314	      exact hbit

   320	      heteroKron (signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i))
   321	        constraintBitSum) 1 := by
   322	  rw [msCellObsA, msCellObsA, msCellObsA, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
   323	    signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A S _),
   324	    signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A S _), mul_one, one_mul]
   325	  rfl

   350	/-- Each of the six row and column relations holds for Alice's cell reflections
   351	on the dilated state, with the sign prescribed by the corresponding linear
   352	equation and with error `12 * sqrt ε`.  This is the first operator consequence
   353	of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. -/
   354	theorem msCellObsA_prod_close (S : Strategy msGame) (ε : ℝ) (hwin : 1 - ε ≤ S.value)
   355	    (i : Fin 6) :
   356	    NormCloseOn (msDilatedStrategy S).ψ (12 * Real.sqrt ε)
   357	      (msCellObsA S i 0 * msCellObsA S i 1 * msCellObsA S i 2)
   358	      (((bitSign (msParity i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • 1) := by

   442	any order in which the three positions occur once each, is the reflection
   443	attached to the sum of the three reported bits. -/
   444	theorem msCellObsA_prod_of (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) (k₀ k₁ k₂ : Fin 3)
   445	    (hsum : ∀ a, constraintBitOrZero k₀ a + constraintBitOrZero k₁ a +
   446	      constraintBitOrZero k₂ a = constraintBitSum a) :
   447	    msCellObsA S i k₀ * msCellObsA S i k₁ * msCellObsA S i k₂ =
   448	      heteroKron (signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i))
   449	        constraintBitSum) 1 := by
   450	  have hkey : signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i))
   451	        (constraintBitOrZero k₀) *
   452	      signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i)) (constraintBitOrZero k₁) *
   453	      signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i)) (constraintBitOrZero k₂) =
   454	      signObs ((msDilatedStrategy S).A (MsType.constraint i)) constraintBitSum := by
   455	    rw [signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A S _),
   456	      signObs_mul _ (msDilatedStrategy_isProjective_A S _)]
   457	    congr 1
   458	    funext a
   459	    exact hsum a
   460	  rw [msCellObsA, msCellObsA, msCellObsA, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul]
   461	  simp only [mul_one]
   462	  rw [hkey]
