   431	/-! ## Row and column parity products -/
   432	
   433	/-- The real sign `(-1)^b` associated with a binary answer. -/
   434	def bitSign (b : ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
   435	  (-1 : ℝ) ^ b.val
   436	
   437	/-- The binary sign turns addition into multiplication. -/
   438	theorem bit_sign_add (b c : ZMod 2) :
   439	    bitSign (b + c) = bitSign b * bitSign c := by
   440	  unfold bitSign
   441	  rw [ZMod.val_add]
   442	  rw [← neg_one_pow_eq_pow_mod_two]
   443	  exact pow_add _ _ _
   444	
   445	/-- The sign of a three-bit parity is the product of the three signs. -/
   446	theorem bit_sign_sum_fin_three (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2) :
   447	    bitSign (∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = ∏ k : Fin 3, bitSign (β k) := by
   448	  rw [Fin.sum_univ_three, Fin.prod_univ_three, bit_sign_add, bit_sign_add]
   449	
   450	/-- A binary sign is never zero. -/
   451	theorem bit_sign_ne_zero (b : ZMod 2) : bitSign b ≠ 0 := by
   452	  unfold bitSign
   453	  exact pow_ne_zero _ (by norm_num)
   454	
   455	/-- The product of the three output signs, with malformed constraint answers
   456	assigned zero so that they remain parity failures. -/
   457	def constraintParityProduct : MsAnswer → ℝ
   458	  | .triple β => ∏ k : Fin 3, bitSign (β k)
   459	  | .bit _ => 0
   460	
   461	/-- Failure of the required sign product for one row or column constraint. -/
   462	def ConstraintParityFailure (i : Fin 6) (a : MsAnswer) : Prop :=
   463	  constraintParityProduct a ≠ bitSign (msParity i)
   464	
   465	/-- Equality of the real parity signs is classically decidable on the finite
   466	Magic Square answer alphabet. -/
   467	noncomputable instance (i : Fin 6) : DecidablePred (ConstraintParityFailure i) :=
   468	  fun a => Classical.propDecidable (ConstraintParityFailure i a)
   469	
   470	/-- Every wrong-form constraint answer is included in the parity-failure event. -/
   471	theorem wrong_constraint_answer_implies_parity_failure (i : Fin 6) (a : MsAnswer)
   472	    (ha : wrongConstraintAnswer a = true) : ConstraintParityFailure i a := by
   473	  cases a with
   474	  | triple β => simp [wrongConstraintAnswer] at ha
   475	  | bit γ =>
   476	      unfold ConstraintParityFailure constraintParityProduct
   477	      exact (bit_sign_ne_zero (msParity i)).symm
   478	
   479	/-- Alice's local failure mass for the row or column sign product. -/
   480	noncomputable def aliceParityFailureMass (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) : ℝ :=
   481	  aliceEventWeight S (.constraint i) (ConstraintParityFailure i)
   482	
   483	/-- Bob's local failure mass for the row or column sign product. -/
   484	noncomputable def bobParityFailureMass (S : Strategy msGame) (i : Fin 6) : ℝ :=
   485	  bobEventWeight S (.constraint i) (ConstraintParityFailure i)
   486	
   487	/-- Alice's malformed constraint mass is part of her parity-failure mass. -/
   488	theorem alice_constraint_wrong_form_mass_le_parity_failure_mass (S : Strategy msGame)
   489	    (i : Fin 6) : aliceConstraintWrongFormMass S i ≤ aliceParityFailureMass S i := by
   490	  unfold aliceConstraintWrongFormMass aliceParityFailureMass
   491	  rw [← outcome_event_weight_left_eq S (.constraint i) (.var (msConstraintVars i 0))]
   492	  rw [← outcome_event_weight_left_eq S (.constraint i) (.var (msConstraintVars i 0))]
   493	  exact outcome_event_weight_mono S _ _ _ _ fun a _ ha =>
   494	    wrong_constraint_answer_implies_parity_failure i a ha
   495	
   496	/-- Bob's malformed constraint mass is part of his parity-failure mass. -/
   497	theorem bob_constraint_wrong_form_mass_le_parity_failure_mass (S : Strategy msGame)
   498	    (i : Fin 6) : bobConstraintWrongFormMass S i ≤ bobParityFailureMass S i := by
   499	  unfold bobConstraintWrongFormMass bobParityFailureMass
   500	  rw [← outcome_event_weight_right_eq S (.var (msConstraintVars i 0)) (.constraint i)]
   501	  rw [← outcome_event_weight_right_eq S (.var (msConstraintVars i 0)) (.constraint i)]
   502	  exact outcome_event_weight_mono S _ _ _ _ fun _ b hb =>
   503	    wrong_constraint_answer_implies_parity_failure i b hb
   504	
   505	private theorem forward_parity_failure_rejects (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3)
   506	    (a b : MsAnswer) (hparity : ConstraintParityFailure i a) :
   507	    msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) a b = false := by
   508	  cases a with
   509	  | bit δ => rfl
   510	  | triple β =>
   511	      cases b with
   512	      | triple βb => rfl
   513	      | bit γ =>
   514	          rw [msWinPredicate, decide_eq_false_iff_not]
   515	          intro haccept
   516	          apply hparity
   517	          unfold constraintParityProduct
   518	          calc
   519	            (∏ l : Fin 3, bitSign (β l)) = bitSign (∑ l : Fin 3, β l) :=
   520	              (bit_sign_sum_fin_three β).symm
   521	            _ = bitSign (msParity i) := by rw [haccept.1]
   522	
   523	private theorem reverse_parity_failure_rejects (i : Fin 6) (k : Fin 3)
   524	    (a b : MsAnswer) (hparity : ConstraintParityFailure i b) :
   525	    msWinPredicate (.var (msConstraintVars i k)) (.constraint i) a b = false := by
   526	  cases a with
   527	  | triple α => rfl
   528	  | bit γ =>
   529	      cases b with
   530	      | bit δ => rfl
   531	      | triple β =>
   532	          rw [msWinPredicate, decide_eq_false_iff_not]
   533	          intro haccept
   534	          apply hparity
   535	          unfold constraintParityProduct
   536	          calc
   537	            (∏ l : Fin 3, bitSign (β l)) = bitSign (∑ l : Fin 3, β l) :=
   538	              (bit_sign_sum_fin_three β).symm
   539	            _ = bitSign (msParity i) := by rw [haccept.1]

     4	/-!
     5	# Reflections and the state-dependent metric on operators
     6	
     7	The self-testing argument for the Magic Square game manipulates `±1`-valued
     8	observables rather than positive operator valued measures.  This file records
     9	the algebra of such observables and the estimates that convert Born masses into
    10	operator bounds.
    11	
    12	Postprocessing a projective measurement along a binary relabelling of its
    13	answers produces a *reflection*, that is, a self-adjoint involution; two
    14	reflections coming from one and the same measurement commute, and their product
    15	is the reflection attached to the sum of the two relabellings.  The reflections
    16	of the source are the binary observables of the rest of the development, so this
    17	file uses `MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable` and its algebra, defined in
    18	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Defs.lean`, rather than a second predicate of
    19	its own.  Two operators are compared through the norm of the difference of their
    20	actions on a fixed state, the relation `NormCloseOn` below.  That relation is the
    21	unsquared Euclidean distance between `M ψ` and `N ψ`; it is *not* the
    22	state-dependent distance `≈_δ` of the source, which bounds the squared quantity
    23	`⟨ψ|(M - N)ᴴ (M - N)|ψ⟩` and is formalized in this development by `opDistSq`.
    24	The comparison is symmetric, satisfies the triangle inequality, and is unchanged
    25	by multiplication on the left by an isometric operator; `NormCloseOn.opDistSq_le`
    26	converts it into the source's relation.  Finally, a real spectral combination of
    27	the joint effects of the two players has state-dependent norm controlled by the
    28	Born mass of the answer pairs carrying a nonzero coefficient; this is the step
    29	that turns each rejection mass of the value-to-parity layer into an operator
    30	estimate.

    37	proved in Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9.

    84	variable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

    86	/-- Formalization-only: the action of an operator on a state is homogeneous. -/
    87	theorem applyOperatorToState_smul (c : ℂ) (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    88	    applyOperatorToState (c • M) ψ = c • applyOperatorToState M ψ := by
    89	  unfold applyOperatorToState
    90	  simp only [map_smul, LinearMap.smul_apply]
    91	
    92	/-- Formalization-only: the zero operator annihilates every state; the
    93	companion `applyOperatorToState_zero` annihilates the zero state instead. -/
    94	theorem applyOperatorToState_zero_op (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    95	    applyOperatorToState (0 : Op ι) ψ = 0 := by
    96	  unfold applyOperatorToState
    97	  simp only [map_zero, LinearMap.zero_apply]
    98	
    99	/-- Formalization-only: acting by a finite sum of operators is the sum of the
   100	actions. -/
   101	theorem applyOperatorToState_sum {γ : Type} [Fintype γ]
   102	    (M : γ → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   103	    applyOperatorToState (∑ c, M c) ψ = ∑ c, applyOperatorToState (M c) ψ := by
   104	  unfold applyOperatorToState
   105	  simp only [map_sum, LinearMap.sum_apply]
   106	
   107	/-- An isometric operator preserves the norm of every state. -/
   108	theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_of_isometry {U : Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1)
   109	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ‖applyOperatorToState U ψ‖ = ‖ψ‖ := by
   110	  have h : ‖applyOperatorToState U ψ‖ ^ 2 = ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   111	    rw [norm_applyOperatorToState_sq, hU, @norm_sq_eq_re_inner ℂ,
   112	      applyOperatorToState_one]
   113	    rfl
   114	  have h1 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState U ψ‖ := norm_nonneg _
   115	  have h2 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ ‖ψ‖ := norm_nonneg _
   116	  nlinarith [h, h1, h2]
   117	
   118	/-- Multiplying on the left by an isometric operator does not change the
   119	state-dependent norm. -/
   120	theorem norm_applyOperatorToState_isometry_mul {U : Op ι} (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1)
   121	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   122	    ‖applyOperatorToState (U * M) ψ‖ = ‖applyOperatorToState M ψ‖ := by
   123	  rw [applyOperatorToState_mul, norm_applyOperatorToState_of_isometry hU]
   124

   127	/-! ## Reflections
   128	
   129	The *reflections* of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   130	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:228-250`, are the self-adjoint involutions attached to
   131	two-outcome projective measurements, which are exactly the binary observables
   132	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable` of
   133	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Linearity/Defs.lean`.  The Magic Square rigidity
   134	argument therefore uses that predicate and its algebra directly:
   135	`IsBinaryObservable.one`, `IsBinaryObservable.mul`,
   136	`IsBinaryObservable.isometry`, `isBinaryObservable_heteroKron_one` and
   137	`isBinaryObservable_one_heteroKron`. -/
   138	
   139	/-- Operators placed on the two tensor factors commute. -/
   140	theorem heteroKron_comm {ιA ιB : Type} [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
   141	    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB] (X : Op ιA) (Y : Op ιB) :
   142	    heteroKron X (1 : Op ιB) * heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) Y =
   143	      heteroKron (1 : Op ιA) Y * heteroKron X (1 : Op ιB) := by
   144	  rw [heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one, one_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
   145	
   146	/-! ## Closeness in the state-dependent norm -/
   147	
   148	/-- Two operators are *close within `δ` on `ψ`* when the state-dependent norm of
   149	their difference is at most `δ`, that is, when the Euclidean distance between
   150	`M ψ` and `N ψ` is at most `δ`.
   151	
   152	This is **not** the relation `M ≈_δ N` of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   153	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:249`, paper
   154	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:644-646`: there the relation
   155	bounds the *squared* quantity `⟨ψ|(M - N)ᴴ (M - N)|ψ⟩` by `O(δ)`, and it is
   156	formalized in this development by `opDistSq` (`def:povm-distance`, blueprint
   157	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`).  The unsquared relation defined here is the one
   158	under which the triangle inequality is additive, which is what the
   159	solution-group computation of `Rigidity/Anticommutation.lean` iterates;
   160	`NormCloseOn.opDistSq_le` converts a bound at scale `δ` here into the bound `δ ^ 2`
   161	for `opDistSq`. -/
   162	def NormCloseOn {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   163	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) (M N : Op ι) : Prop :=
   164	  ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ≤ δ
   165	
   166	namespace NormCloseOn
   167	
   168	variable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   169	variable {ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι} {δ η : ℝ} {M N P U : Op ι}
   170	
   171	/-- Equal operators are close at every nonnegative scale. -/
   172	theorem of_eq (h : M = N) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N := by
   173	  have hzero : applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ = 0 := by
   174	    rw [h, sub_self, applyOperatorToState_zero_op]
   175	  rw [NormCloseOn, hzero, norm_zero]
   176	  exact hδ
   177	
   178	/-- Closeness is symmetric. -/
   179	theorem symm (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) : NormCloseOn ψ δ N M := by
   180	  have happ : applyOperatorToState (N - M) ψ = -applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ := by
   181	    rw [show N - M = -(M - N) by abel]
   182	    unfold applyOperatorToState
   183	    simp only [map_neg, LinearMap.neg_apply]
   184	  rw [NormCloseOn, happ, norm_neg]
   185	  exact h
   186	
   187	/-- Enlarging the scale preserves closeness. -/
   188	theorem mono (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) (hδ : δ ≤ η) : NormCloseOn ψ η M N :=
   189	  le_trans h hδ
   190	
   191	/-- Closeness composes by the triangle inequality. -/
   192	theorem trans (h₁ : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) (h₂ : NormCloseOn ψ η N P) :
   193	    NormCloseOn ψ (δ + η) M P := by
   194	  have hsplit : M - P = (M - N) + (N - P) := by abel
   195	  calc ‖applyOperatorToState (M - P) ψ‖
   196	      = ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ + applyOperatorToState (N - P) ψ‖ := by
   197	        rw [hsplit, applyOperatorToState_add_op]
   198	    _ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ + ‖applyOperatorToState (N - P) ψ‖ :=
   199	        norm_add_le _ _
   200	    _ ≤ δ + η := add_le_add h₁ h₂
   201	
   202	/-- Multiplying on the left by an isometric operator preserves closeness. -/
   203	theorem isometry_mul (hU : Uᴴ * U = 1) (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) :
   204	    NormCloseOn ψ δ (U * M) (U * N) := by
   205	  have hsub : U * M - U * N = U * (M - N) := by noncomm_ring
   206	  rw [NormCloseOn, hsub, norm_applyOperatorToState_isometry_mul hU]
   207	  exact h
   208	
   209	/-- Negating both operators leaves the state-dependent norm of the difference
   210	unchanged. -/
   211	theorem neg (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) : NormCloseOn ψ δ (-M) (-N) := by
   212	  change ‖applyOperatorToState (-M - -N) ψ‖ ≤ δ
   213	  rw [show -M - -N = -(M - N) by abel]
   214	  have happ : applyOperatorToState (-(M - N)) ψ =
   215	      -applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ := by
   216	    unfold applyOperatorToState
   217	    simp only [map_neg, LinearMap.neg_apply]
   218	  rw [happ, norm_neg]
   219	  exact h
   220	
   221	/-- Multiplying both operators by a scalar of modulus one leaves the
   222	state-dependent norm of the difference unchanged. -/
   223	theorem smul {c : ℂ} (hc : ‖c‖ = 1) (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) :
   224	    NormCloseOn ψ δ (c • M) (c • N) := by
   225	  change ‖applyOperatorToState (c • M - c • N) ψ‖ ≤ δ
   226	  rw [← smul_sub, applyOperatorToState_smul, norm_smul, hc, one_mul]
   227	  exact h
   228	
   229	/-- Replacing the left factor of a product costs the distance between the two
   230	factors plus twice the cost of replacing the right factor by an operator
   231	commuting with both.  This is the mechanism by which a state-dependent relation
   232	is used in the middle of a word: the tail is first moved to the other player,
   233	where it commutes with everything acting on the first player. -/
   234	theorem mul_left_subst {X X' K K' : Op ι}
   235	    (hXX' : NormCloseOn ψ δ X X') (hKK' : NormCloseOn ψ η K K')
   236	    (hX : Xᴴ * X = 1) (hX' : X'ᴴ * X' = 1) (hK' : K'ᴴ * K' = 1)
   237	    (hcX : X * K' = K' * X) (hcX' : X' * K' = K' * X') :
   238	    NormCloseOn ψ (η + δ + η) (X * K) (X' * K) := by
   239	  have h1 : NormCloseOn ψ η (X * K) (X * K') := NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hX hKK'
   240	  have h2 : NormCloseOn ψ δ (X * K') (X' * K') := by
   241	    change ‖applyOperatorToState (X * K' - X' * K') ψ‖ ≤ δ
   242	    rw [show X * K' - X' * K' = K' * X - K' * X' by rw [hcX, hcX']]
   243	    exact NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hK' hXX'
   244	  have h3 : NormCloseOn ψ η (X' * K') (X' * K) := NormCloseOn.isometry_mul hX' hKK'.symm
   245	  exact (h1.trans h2).trans h3
   246	
   247	/-- Conversion to the state-dependent distance of the source: `M ≈_δ N` of
   248	`thm:ms-rigidity` (blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:249`, paper
   249	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:644-646`) bounds
   250	`⟨ψ|(M - N)ᴴ (M - N)|ψ⟩`, which is `opDistSq` on the one-point distribution
   251	(`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`).  A bound at
   252	scale `δ` for the unsquared relation is a bound at scale `δ ^ 2` for it. -/
   253	theorem opDistSq_le (h : NormCloseOn ψ δ M N) :
   254	    opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => M) (fun _ => N) ψ ≤ δ ^ 2 := by
   255	  have hnorm : ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ≤ δ := h
   256	  have heq : opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => M) (fun _ => N) ψ =
   257	      ‖applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
   258	    rw [opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq, opFamilyDistSq_uniform_unit]
   259	    simp
   260	  rw [heq]
   261	  nlinarith [norm_nonneg (applyOperatorToState (M - N) ψ)]
   262	
   263	end NormCloseOn

   265	/-! ## Sign observables of a projective measurement -/
   266	
   267	section SignObs
   268	
   269	variable {α d : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   270	
   270	
   271	/-- The `±1`-valued observable attached to a measurement together with a binary
   272	relabelling of its answers: an answer labelled `0` carries the eigenvalue `1`
   273	and an answer labelled `1` carries the eigenvalue `-1`.  For the Magic Square
   274	these are the cell observables of `thm:ms-rigidity`, blueprint
   275	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`, paper
   276	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`. -/
   277	noncomputable def signObs (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) (f : α → ZMod 2) : Op d :=
   278	  ∑ a, (bitSign (f a) : ℂ) • M.effect a
   279	
   280	/-- The sign observable is the observable of the binary measurement obtained by
   281	relabelling the answers. -/
   282	theorem signObs_eq_obsOf_postprocess (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   283	    (f : α → ZMod 2) : signObs M f = obsOf (M.postprocess f) := by
   284	  classical
   285	  have hcases : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x = 0 ∨ x = 1 := by decide
   286	  have key : ∀ a : α, (bitSign (f a) : ℂ) • M.effect a =
   287	      (if f a = 0 then M.effect a else 0) - (if f a = 1 then M.effect a else 0) := by
   288	    intro a
   289	    rcases hcases (f a) with h | h <;> rw [h] <;>
   290	      norm_num [bitSign, ZMod.val_one, neg_one_smul]
   291	  rw [signObs, obsOf, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
   292	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter,
   293	    Finset.sum_filter, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
   294	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => key a
   295	
   296	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   297	/-- Formalization-only: the effects of a projective measurement are mutually
   298	orthogonal, so two spectral combinations of them multiply coefficientwise. -/
   299	private theorem sum_smul_effect_mul (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   300	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (c e : α → ℂ) :
   301	    (∑ a, c a • M.effect a) * (∑ a, e a • M.effect a) =
   302	      ∑ a, (c a * e a) • M.effect a := by
   303	  classical
   304	  have horth : ∀ a b : α, a ≠ b → M.effect a * M.effect b = 0 := fun a b hab =>
   305	    mul_eq_zero_of_isProj_family hM M.sum_le_one hab
   306	  rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   307	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   308	  have hidem : M.effect a * M.effect a = M.effect a := (hM a).isIdempotentElem
   309	  rw [Matrix.smul_mul, Matrix.mul_sum, Finset.smul_sum, Finset.sum_eq_single a]
   310	  · rw [Matrix.mul_smul, smul_smul, hidem]
   311	  · intro b _ hba
   312	    rw [Matrix.mul_smul, horth a b (Ne.symm hba), smul_zero, smul_zero]
   313	  · intro ha
   314	    exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ a) ha
   315	
   316	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   317	/-- Sign observables of one projective measurement multiply by adding their
   318	relabellings. -/
   319	theorem signObs_mul (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   320	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f g : α → ZMod 2) :
   321	    signObs M f * signObs M g = signObs M (fun a => f a + g a) := by
   322	  rw [signObs, signObs, sum_smul_effect_mul M hM, signObs]
   323	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   324	  rw [← Complex.ofReal_mul, ← bit_sign_add]
   325	
   326	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   327	/-- The sign observable of the zero relabelling is the identity. -/
   328	theorem signObs_const_zero (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d) :
   329	    signObs M (fun _ => 0) = 1 := by
   330	  have hb : ((bitSign (0 : ZMod 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) = 1 := by norm_num [bitSign]
   331	  rw [signObs]
   332	  simp only [hb, one_smul]
   333	  exact M.sum_eq_one
   334	
   335	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   336	/-- A sign observable of a projective measurement is an involution. -/
   337	theorem signObs_mul_self (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   338	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
   339	    signObs M f * signObs M f = 1 := by
   340	  rw [signObs_mul M hM]
   341	  have hzero : (fun a => f a + f a) = fun _ : α => (0 : ZMod 2) := by
   342	    funext a
   343	    exact (by decide : ∀ x : ZMod 2, x + x = 0) (f a)
   344	  rw [hzero, signObs_const_zero]
   345	
   346	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   347	/-- A sign observable of a projective measurement is self-adjoint. -/
   348	theorem signObs_conjTranspose (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   349	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
   350	    (signObs M f)ᴴ = signObs M f := by
   351	  rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, signObs, star_sum]
   352	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   353	  rw [star_smul]
   354	  congr 1
   355	  · simp
   356	  · exact (hM a).isSelfAdjoint
   357	
   358	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   359	/-- A sign observable of a projective measurement is a binary observable, the
   360	reflection attached to the relabelling `f`. -/
   361	theorem isBinaryObservable_signObs (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   362	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f : α → ZMod 2) :
   363	    IsBinaryObservable (signObs M f) :=
   364	  ⟨signObs_conjTranspose M hM f, signObs_mul_self M hM f⟩
   365	
   366	omit [DecidableEq α] in
   367	/-- Sign observables of one projective measurement commute. -/
   368	theorem signObs_comm (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   369	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (f g : α → ZMod 2) :
   370	    signObs M f * signObs M g = signObs M g * signObs M f := by
   371	  rw [signObs_mul M hM, signObs_mul M hM]
   372	  congr 1
   373	  funext a
   374	  exact add_comm _ _
   375	
   376	end SignObs

   378	/-! ## Deviation of joint spectral combinations on the strategy state -/
   379	
   380	section JointDefect
   381	
   382	/-- Formalization-only: scalars pass through the second tensor factor. -/
   383	theorem heteroKron_smul_right {ιA ιB : Type} (c : ℂ) (M : Op ιA) (N : Op ιB) :
   384	    heteroKron M (c • N) = c • heteroKron M N := by
   385	  unfold heteroKron
   386	  exact Matrix.kronecker_smul c M N
   387	
   388	/-- Formalization-only: a real spectral combination of the effects of a
   389	projective measurement is self-adjoint. -/
   390	private theorem sum_real_smul_effect_conjTranspose {α d : Type} [Fintype α]
   391	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement α d)
   392	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) (c : α → ℝ) :
   393	    (∑ a, ((c a : ℝ) : ℂ) • M.effect a)ᴴ = ∑ a, ((c a : ℝ) : ℂ) • M.effect a := by
   394	  rw [← Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, star_sum]
   395	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   396	  rw [star_smul]
   397	  congr 1
   398	  · simp
   399	  · exact (hM a).isSelfAdjoint
   400	
   401	/-- Formalization-only: the quadratic form of a real spectral combination on a
   402	state is the corresponding real combination of the individual quadratic
   403	forms. -/
   404	private theorem re_inner_apply_sum_real_smul {ι γ : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   405	    [Fintype γ] (r : γ → ℝ) (K : γ → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :

    fix(review): faithful closeness convention for the rigidity chain (PR 162 round 2)
    
    F1: delete the pass-through abbreviation `IsReflection`; its explanatory
    prose becomes the `## Reflections` section comment, which keeps pointing
    readers at `MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable`.
    
    F2: the state-dependent relation of `Rigidity/Reflections.lean` bounds the
    unsquared norm, while `M ~_delta N` of `thm:ms-rigidity` (blueprint
    `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:249`, paper
    `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:644-646`) bounds the squared
    quantity. Rename `CloseOn` to `NormCloseOn`, state in its docstring and in
    the module docstring what it is and what it is not, and add the explicit
    conversion `NormCloseOn.opDistSq_le` into `opDistSq`, the formal counterpart
    of the source's relation (`def:povm-distance`). The anticommutation
    docstrings no longer claim to be the source's relation, and
    `msVarObsA_anticommute_opDistSq` / `msVarObsB_anticommute_opDistSq` record
    the source's own form at the printed scale `sqrt eps` for `eps <= 1`. No
    paper-labelled statement is weakened: the norm bound `624 * sqrt eps` gives
    the squared bound `624 ^ 2 * eps`, which is stronger than the printed
    `O(sqrt eps)` in that range.
    
    F3: `NormCloseOn.neg`, `NormCloseOn.smul` and `NormCloseOn.mul_left_subst`
    move from `Rigidity/Anticommutation.lean` and `Rigidity/CellRelations.lean`
    to the module that defines the relation.
    
    F4: delete `isProj_heteroKron` and use the imported
    `MakingMeasurementsProjective.isProj_kronecker`.

references/cs-paper/Arxiv v2 - Robust LCS self testing/introduction.tex:1:In \cite{peres1990incompatible,mermin1990simple}, Mermin and Peres discovered an algebraic coincidence related to the $3\times3$ ``Magic Square'' of operators on $\C^2\otimes \C^2$ in Figure \ref{fig:magic-square-operators-introduction}.
references/cs-paper/Arxiv v2 - Robust LCS self testing/introduction.tex:3:If we pick any row and take the product of the three operators in that row (note that they commute, so the order does not matter), we get the identity operator. Similarly, we can try this with the columns. Two of the columns give identity while the other  gives $-1$ times identity. Thus, the product of these nine operators depends on whether they are multiplied row by row or column by column. This can be exploited to define a two-player, one-referee game called the Mermin--Peres Magic Square game \cite{aravind2004quantum} (see Definition \ref{definition:linear-constraint-game} and Figure \ref{fig:magic-square-equations} for a formal definition). Informally, the Mermin--Peres Magic Square game mod $2$ is as follows. The players claim to have a $3\times 3$ square of numbers in which each row and each of the first two columns sums to $0\pmod 2$, while the third column sums to $1\pmod 2$. (The players are usually called ``provers'', since they try to prove that they have such a square.) The referee asks the first player to present a row of the supposed square and the second to present a column. They reply respectively with the $3$ entries of that row and column in $\{0,1\}$. They win if their responses sum to $0$ or $1$ as appropriate, and they give the same number for the entry where the row and column overlap. This game can be won with probability $1$ by provers that share two pairs of maximally entangled qubits of dimension $2$, but provers with no entanglement can win with probability at most $\frac89$. Games which are won in the classical case with probability $< 1$ but are won in the quantum case with probability $1$ are known as \emph{pseudotelepathy games}.
